definition_zh: n. 无政府主义（主张废除国家与强制性等级）
definition_en: The political belief that the state and all coercive hierarchy should be abolished and society organised through voluntary cooperation.
core_image: 把头顶那把椅子搬走，人们自己围成一圈
scene: 这本小册子主张用合作社取代官僚机构。 Anarchism shaped the early labour movement here.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：小册子主张废除强制性的国家机构，由自愿合作来组织社会，这就是 anarchism 的核心主张。

pos.zh: 无政府主义

collocations.zh: 无政府主义与社会主义

senses.title: The political doctrine
senses.definition: the belief that coercive government should be replaced by voluntary associations and mutual aid
senses.definitionCN: 主张以自愿结社与互助取代强制性政府的信念
senses.example: Anarchism argues that order need not come from above.
senses.exampleCN: 无政府主义主张秩序不必自上而下产生。
senses.why: Greek an- means without and arkhos means ruler, so the word names a programme of doing without rulers, not a programme of chaos.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 an- 意为「没有」，arkhos 意为「统治者」，所以这个词命名的是一套「不要统治者」的方案，而不是「要混乱」的方案。

senses.title: The historical movement
senses.titleCN: 历史上的无政府主义运动
senses.definition: the body of thought, writers and organisations that carried that doctrine from the nineteenth century onward
senses.definitionCN: 自 19 世纪起承载该学说的思想、作者与组织的总体
senses.example: Spanish anarchism drew millions of workers before the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战前西班牙的无政府主义运动吸引了数百万工人。
senses.why: Once the doctrine had newspapers, unions and congresses, the same word came to name a movement with a history rather than only an idea.
senses.whyCN: 当这套学说有了报纸、工会与代表大会，同一个词便转而指一场有历史的运动，而不只是一个想法。

intro.en: Anarchism is Greek an-, without, plus arkhos, ruler, plus -ism. Proudhon made French anarchisme a positive programme in 1840, turning an old word for disorder into a doctrine.
intro.cn: anarchism 由希腊语 an-「没有」加 arkhos「统治者」加 -ism 构成。蒲鲁东在 1840 年把法语 anarchisme 变成一套正面方案，把一个原指混乱的旧词变成了学说。

items.en: Greek an- means not or without before a vowel, the same prefix that builds anaerobic and anonymous.
items.cn: 希腊语 an- 在元音前意为「不、没有」，与构成 anaerobic 和 anonymous 的是同一前缀。

items.en: Greek arkhos meant leader or ruler, from arkhein, to begin or to rule. It gives monarchy, oligarchy and hierarchy.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhos 意为「首领、统治者」，来自 arkhein「开始、统治」。它产生 monarchy、oligarchy 与 hierarchy。

items.en: Greek anarkhia meant the absence of a ruler, and in Athens it described a year without a chief magistrate, usually with disapproval.
items.cn: 希腊语 anarkhia 意为「没有统治者」，在雅典指没有首席执政官的年份，通常带贬义。

items.en: Proudhon declared himself an anarchist in 1840 and used French anarchisme for a positive order built on contracts and mutual credit.
items.cn: 蒲鲁东在 1840 年自称无政府主义者，并用法语 anarchisme 指建立在契约与互助信贷之上的正面秩序。

items.en: English took anarchism in the mid nineteenth century, and the word now covers both the doctrine and the movements that carried it.
items.cn: 英语在 19 世纪中期借入 anarchism，如今该词既指学说，也指承载它的各场运动。

note.en: The look-alike group separates anarchism from anarchy, which means disorder; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring political currents.
note.cn: 形近组把 anarchism 与意为「混乱」的 anarchy 分开；近义组列出相邻的政治思潮。

entries.definition: A state of disorder without authority.
entries.definitionCN: 没有权威的混乱状态。

entries.definition: A person who believes in anarchism.
entries.definitionCN: 信奉无政府主义的人。

entries.definition: Lawless or wildly disordered.
entries.definitionCN: 无法无天或极度混乱的。

entries.definition: Support for rule by a monarch.
entries.definitionCN: 支持君主统治。

entries.definition: A doctrine of maximal individual liberty.
entries.definitionCN: 主张个人自由最大化的学说。

entries.definition: A doctrine of worker union control.
entries.definitionCN: 主张由工人工会掌控的学说。

entries.definition: A doctrine of common ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 主张共同所有的学说。

entries.definition: The rejection of all established values.
entries.definitionCN: 对一切既有价值的否弃。

normalIntro.en: Anarchism is an- plus arch plus -ism: without rulers, as a programme rather than a mess.
normalIntro.cn: anarchism 就是 an- 加 arch 加 -ism：不要统治者，而且是一套方案，不是一团乱。

normal.en: Anarchism is the doctrine; anarchy is the disorder.
normal.cn: anarchism 是学说，anarchy 是混乱。

normal.en: Arch means ruler, so monarchy is one ruler and anarchism is none.
normal.cn: arch 意为「统治者」，所以 monarchy 是一个统治者，anarchism 是没有。

normal.en: It is uncountable: anarchism, not an anarchism.
normal.cn: 它不可数：anarchism，不说 an anarchism。

normal.en: The person is an anarchist, the adjective anarchic.
normal.cn: 人是 anarchist，形容词是 anarchic。

normal.en: Proudhon turned a negative word into a positive programme in 1840.
normal.cn: 蒲鲁东在 1840 年把一个贬义词变成了正面方案。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where nobody sits at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一场没有人坐在桌首的会议。

abstract.en: Imagine a workshop run by the people who work in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一间由在其中劳动的人共同管理的工场。

abstract.en: Think of a circle of chairs with the throne removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈椅子，中间那把王座被搬走了。

examples.en: Anarchism has always argued about organisation.
examples.cn: 无政府主义内部一直在争论组织问题。

examples.en: The pamphlet traces anarchism back to the 1840s.
examples.cn: 这本小册子把无政府主义追溯到 19 世纪 40 年代。

examples.en: He studied anarchism alongside early socialism.
examples.cn: 他把无政府主义与早期社会主义放在一起研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「无」+ arch「统治者」+ ism「主义」——主张不要统治者的主义，就是无政府主义，别和「混乱」的 anarchy 混。

root: 希腊语 an-「无」+ arkhos「统治者」构成 anarkhia「无统治者」，蒲鲁东 1840 年造法语 anarchisme 赋予正面含义，英语加 -ism 成 anarchism，字面即「无统治者主义」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one rejection of rulers: first the argument itself, then the newspapers, unions and people who carried it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次对统治者的拒斥：先是那套论证本身，再是承载它的报纸、工会与人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chair at the top removed, people in a circle
core.cn: 核心意象：头顶那把椅子被搬走，人们围成一圈

branches.en: A pamphlet against coercive authority.
branches.cn: 一本反对强制权威的小册子。

branches.en: Mutual aid replacing a ministry.
branches.cn: 互助取代一个部门。

branches.en: A workers congress with no chair.
branches.cn: 一场没有主席的工人代表大会。

branches.en: A century of newspapers and unions.
branches.cn: 一个世纪的报纸与工会。

branches.en: One idea, then a body that carried it.
branches.cn: 先是一个想法，再是承载它的群体。

intro.en: Anarchism is an- plus arch plus -ism, and the arch piece alone builds monarchy, oligarchy and hierarchy.
intro.cn: anarchism 是 an- 加 arch 加 -ism，仅 arch 这个部件就构成 monarchy、oligarchy 与 hierarchy。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are Greek an- and arkhos; French anarchisme supplied the modern political sense before English borrowed it.
latinIntro.cn: 部件是希腊语 an- 与 arkhos；法语 anarchisme 先赋予现代政治含义，英语再借入。

definition_zh: 本质上、实质上；概括地说（指撇开细节之后的根本性质）
definition_en: fundamentally; in its true nature, once details are set aside
core_image: 一枚果子削去外皮与果肉，只剩中间那颗核
scene: 两个人争了半天条文措辞，旁人听完只说了一句：争的其实是同一件事。 In essence, the two proposals ask for the same reform.
sceneCN: 这里取「本质上、实质上」（第 1 个义项：撇开细节后的根本性质）；句意为两个提案实质上要求的是同一项改革。

pos.zh: 副词短语：本质上；实质上；概括地说

collocations.phrase: different in form, same in essence

forms.label: 对照形式
forms.form: in form but not in essence

senses.title: The true nature
senses.definition: used to state what something really is once surface differences are removed
senses.definitionCN: 用来陈述剥去表面差异之后某物真正的样子
senses.example: The two systems differ in form but agree in essence.
senses.exampleCN: 两种制度形式不同，本质一致。
senses.why: Essence names the being of a thing, so the phrase reaches past appearance to what remains.
senses.whyCN: 本质指事物的存在本身，因此短语越过表象，指向留下来的东西。

senses.title: Beside the single adverb
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：与单词副词的分工
senses.definition: the frame stands as a sentence adverbial, while the single adverb can sit inside the clause
senses.definitionCN: 这个框架作句子状语，而单词副词可位于小句内部
senses.example: In essence, the complaint is about pay, not hours.
senses.exampleCN: 实质上，抱怨的是薪酬，不是工时。
senses.why: A comment on the whole statement differs from a modifier inside it.
senses.whyCN: 对整句的评述不同于句内的修饰语。

senses.title: At bottom
senses.definition: it reduces a complicated account to its single governing point
senses.definitionCN: 把复杂的叙述归结到那个起支配作用的要点
senses.example: In essence, the change removes one layer of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 归根结底，这项改变去掉了一层审批。
senses.why: Reduction is the work of the phrase: many details, one core.
senses.whyCN: 归约正是这个短语的工作：许多细节，一个核心。

senses.title: A summary opener
senses.definition: at the start of a sentence it announces a compressed restatement of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，预告对前文的压缩重述
senses.example: In essence, the argument rests on a single assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 实质上，这个论证只依赖一个假设。
senses.why: The front slot tells the reader that the next clause is the kernel, not a new detail.
senses.whyCN: 前置位置告诉读者，接下来的小句是内核，而不是新细节。

senses.title: Not principle
senses.definition: it names what a thing is, while the look-alike phrase names what a rule allows in theory
senses.definitionCN: 它指出事物是什么，而形近短语指出规则在理论上允许什么
senses.example: In principle the plan works; in essence it is a copy of the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上这个方案可行；本质上它只是旧方案的翻版。
senses.why: Being and permission are different questions, so the two phrases cannot be swapped.
senses.whyCN: 存在与许可属于不同问题，因此两个短语不能互换。

senses.title: The philosophical use
senses.definition: in philosophy it asks what a thing is apart from its accidents and appearances
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中追问某物除去偶性与表象之后究竟是什么
senses.example: Philosophers ask what a thing is in essence.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问一物本质上是什么。
senses.why: The phrase inherits a technical history, which is why it can sound grave in ordinary prose.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语继承了术语史，因此在普通文字里也会显得庄重。

senses.title: Not the extract
senses.titleCN: 辨义：不表香精或精华液
senses.definition: the noun can name a concentrated substance, but the phrase speaks of abstract nature
senses.definitionCN: 这个名词可指浓缩物，但短语说的是抽象性质
senses.example: The perfume is an essence, but the phrase in essence says something else.
senses.exampleCN: 香水本身是一种香精，但实质上这个短语说的是另一回事。
senses.why: Chemistry gave the noun a concrete sense that the fixed phrase never uses.
senses.whyCN: 化学给了这个名词具体义，而固定短语从不使用它。

senses.title: The closing summary
senses.definition: it can also close a passage, labelling what the whole account amounted to
senses.definitionCN: 也可用在段末，标出整段叙述归结为何
senses.example: Both sides want the same outcome in essence.
senses.exampleCN: 双方实质上想要的是同一个结果。
senses.why: Final position makes the phrase sound like a verdict delivered after the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 末位让这个短语像是听完证据后作出的裁断。

intro.en: Essence comes from Latin essentia, the abstract noun for being, generally attributed to Cicero as a rendering of Greek ousia, from esse, to be. The attribution is the usual one; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: essence 来自拉丁语 essentia，即表存在的抽象名词，一般认为由西塞罗仿希腊语 ousia 所造，词根为 esse「存在」。这一归属是通行说法；短语属近代。

items.en: Esse, to be, is the most basic verb of existence and supplies the stem of the noun.
items.cn: esse 意为存在，是最基本的存在动词，提供这个名词的词干。

items.en: Latin needed a noun for what a thing is, and essentia was coined to fill the gap; the attribution to Cicero is the usual one.
items.cn: 拉丁语需要一个名词来指事物之所是，于是造出 essentia 填补空白；归于西塞罗是通行说法。

items.en: The Greek model named being or substance, and the Latin coinage was meant to match it.
items.cn: 希腊语原型指存在或实体，拉丁语新造词正是为与之对应。

items.en: Scholastic writing fixed the word in arguments about substance and accident.
items.cn: 经院文字把这个词固定在关于实体与偶性的论证中。

items.en: Chemistry later applied the noun to a concentrated substance, a sense the phrase ignores.
items.cn: 化学后来用这个名词指浓缩物，短语并不采用这一义。

items.en: The summarising frame belongs to modern prose; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个概括框架属于近代文字，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the form or the abstract register but differs in what it names; the second group are one-word equivalents of the core sense.
note.cn: 第一组共用形式或抽象语域，但所指不同；第二组是核心意义的单词对应说法。

entries.definition: It concerns the main content of a claim, often in legal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 它指主张的主要内容，多用于法律文字。

entries.definition: It means vitally important, often of timing in a contract.
entries.definitionCN: 意为至关重要，常指合同中的时限。

entries.definition: It means in practice or as good as, not in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 意为实际上、等于，而非本质上。

entries.definition: It marks something that exists as a label rather than in fact.
entries.definitionCN: 标出只在名目上而非事实上存在的东西。

entries.definition: A single adverb with the same reduction to the core.
entries.definitionCN: 单词副词，同样归结到核心。

entries.definition: It means fundamentally, with an image of depth.
entries.definitionCN: 意为根本上，带深浅意象。

entries.definition: It points to the base on which a thing rests.
entries.definitionCN: 指向事物所依托的根基。

entries.definition: The everyday word for reducing a matter to essentials.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题归到要点的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real verb of being, the coined Latin noun, and the real split from principle and from the chemical extract.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的存在动词、拉丁语新造名词，以及与原则义、化学浓缩物义的分工。

normal.en: The root is simply to be, so the phrase asks what a thing is.
normal.cn: 词根就是存在，因此短语追问事物是什么。

normal.en: Latin coined the noun to name being, and the coinage is usually credited to Cicero.
normal.cn: 拉丁语造出这个名词来指存在，通常归功于西塞罗。

normal.en: It stands as a comment on the whole sentence, not on one word.
normal.cn: 它评述整句，而非某一个词。

normal.en: Principle concerns what is allowed in theory; essence concerns what a thing is.
normal.cn: 原则关心理论上允许什么，本质关心事物是什么。

normal.en: The chemical sense of a concentrated extract never enters the phrase.
normal.cn: 化学上的浓缩物义从不进入这个短语。

abstract.en: Like a fruit pared down to the stone at its centre.
abstract.cn: 像果子削到只剩中间那颗核。

abstract.en: Like a long letter reduced to the one sentence that mattered.
abstract.cn: 像一封长信压缩成唯一要紧的那句话。

abstract.en: Like a building stripped of its paint, showing only the frame.
abstract.cn: 像剥去漆面的建筑，只剩骨架。

examples.en: In essence, the two plans are the same.
examples.cn: 实质上，两个方案是一样的。

examples.en: The dispute is in essence about water rights.
examples.cn: 这场争端实质上是关于水权。

examples.en: In essence, nothing in the procedure has changed.
examples.cn: 实质上，程序没有任何改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因 伊森斯」——果子削到只剩中间那颗核：本质上

root: 核心名词意为本质，出自拉丁语 essentia「存在、本质」，一般认为由西塞罗仿希腊语 ousia 所造，词根为 esse「存在」。该短语为近代书面语定型，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the true nature, the boundary against the single adverb, reduction to the governing point, the summary opener, the contrast with principle, the philosophical use, the exclusion of the extract and the closing verdict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项涵盖：根本性质、与单词副词的语法边界、归结到支配要点、概述开篇、与原则的对照、哲学用法、排除浓缩物义，以及句末裁断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fruit pared of skin and flesh until only the stone at its centre remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚果子削去皮与肉，只剩中间那颗核。

branches.en: THE NATURE: what a thing is, once appearances and accidents are removed.
branches.cn: 性质：剥去表象与偶性之后，事物之所是。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: a comment on the whole clause differs from a modifier inside it.
branches.cn: 语法：评述整句不同于句内修饰语。

branches.en: THE REDUCTION: many details are compressed into one kernel, announced at the front.
branches.cn: 归约：许多细节压缩成一个内核，并在句首先行宣告。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: a thing's being is not the permission a rule gives.
branches.cn: 对照：事物的存在不同于规则给出的许可。

branches.en: THE LIMIT AND THE VERDICT: the chemical extract is excluded, and the phrase may close a passage.
branches.cn: 边界与裁断：排除化学浓缩物，且可用于段末收束。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin noun coined from the verb to be, so its core is existence rather than appearance.
intro.cn: 这个短语建在一个由存在动词造出的拉丁语名词上，因此其核心是存在而非表象。

latinIntro.en: Latin esse, to be, produced essentia, a coinage usually credited to Cicero for rendering Greek ousia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 esse「存在」造出 essentia，这一新造词通常归功于西塞罗，用来对应希腊语 ousia。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
The noun was made to name what a thing is.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词被造来指事物之所是。

items.example: English keeps both the abstract and the chemical senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语兼留抽象义与化学义。

items.example: The adjective marks what the nature cannot lack.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标出性质所不能缺少的东西。

items.example: The adverb reduces a matter to its core.
The plural gathers what cannot be dropped.
items.exampleCN: 复数汇集不能省略的东西。

items.meaning: the fifth essence; the purest form
items.example: The compound adds a fifth element to the four of older physics.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词在旧物理的四元素之外加上第五种。

items.example: The frame is standard in summary and verdict.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架是概括与裁断的标准形式。

items.example: The other frame turns essence into urgency.
items.exampleCN: 另一个框架把本质转为紧迫。

a deficit in the balance of trade

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多国或多期差额）

derivatives.zh: 平衡；余额；使平衡（短语的核心名词，语义为两端相等或相减后的余数）
均衡的（balance 加形容词后缀，指两侧相称）
失衡的（un- 加 balanced，指两侧不相称）
贸易；交易（短语的限定成分，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）
交易活动（trade 加动名词后缀，指持续的买卖）

senses.title: The net difference between exports and imports
senses.definition: the difference between the total value of goods exported and the total value of goods imported in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内货物出口总值与进口总值的差
senses.example: The quarterly balance of trade moved into surplus for the first time.
senses.exampleCN: 该季度的贸易差额首次转为顺差。
senses.why: Latin bilanx is 'two scales', and a balance is the beam between them; applied to trade, the beam settles according to which side is heavier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 bilanx 意为「两只有秤盘的天平」，balance 就是那根横梁；用在贸易上，横梁按哪一侧更重而停住。

senses.title: The statistical record of that difference
senses.titleCN: 记录这一差额的统计账目
senses.definition: the official account or statement that records exports and imports and their net result
senses.definitionCN: 记录进出口及其净结果的官方账目或报表
senses.example: The balance of trade is published every month.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易差额每月公布。
senses.why: A balance can be a document as well as a quantity, so the phrase names the published account itself.
senses.whyCN: balance 既可指数量，也可指文件，因此这个短语也指公布的那份账目。

senses.title: The balance in goods alone
senses.definition: the balance measured on merchandise only, as distinct from goods and services together
senses.definitionCN: 只按商品计算、与货物和服务合计相区别的差额
senses.example: The balance of trade in goods differs from the services account.
senses.exampleCN: 货物贸易差额与服务账目并不相同。
senses.why: Statistical systems keep separate ledgers, so the phrase is often qualified by the item being counted.
senses.whyCN: 统计体系分设账目，因此这个短语常被限定为所计的项目。

senses.title: A favourable or unfavourable balance
senses.definition: the older usage in which a surplus is called favourable and a deficit unfavourable
senses.definitionCN: 旧时把顺差称为有利、把逆差称为不利的用法
senses.example: Mercantilists prized a favourable balance of trade above all.
senses.exampleCN: 重商主义者把出超看得高于一切。
senses.why: Before statistics was neutral, the balance was judged by policy advantage, so one sign was praised and the other blamed.
senses.whyCN: 在统计尚未中性化之前，差额要按政策利害评判，因此一个符号受褒，另一个受贬。

senses.title: The balance as a policy indicator
senses.titleCN: 作为政策指标的贸易差额
senses.definition: the balance read as a signal of competitiveness, demand or external vulnerability
senses.definitionCN: 被读作竞争力、需求或对外脆弱性信号的差额
senses.example: A widening deficit in the balance of trade alarmed the treasury.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易差额逆差扩大使财政部警觉。
senses.why: A single number is easy to cite, so the balance became a shorthand for the health of external trade.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字便于引用，于是贸易差额成了对外贸健康与否的简称。

senses.title: The period figure as published
senses.definition: the balance reported for a month, quarter or year
senses.definitionCN: 按月、按季或按年报告的那一差额
senses.example: The monthly balance of trade beat expectations.
senses.exampleCN: 月度贸易差额好于预期。
senses.why: Because the balance is recalculated each period, the phrase often carries month, quarter or year as a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 因为差额按期重算，这个短语常带月份、季度或年份作限定。

senses.title: Adjusting or correcting the balance
senses.definition: the balance considered as something to be improved by tariffs, currency or spending policy
senses.definitionCN: 被视为可通过关税、汇率或支出政策加以改善的差额
senses.example: The government tried to correct the balance of trade with tariffs.
senses.exampleCN: 政府试图用关税纠正贸易差额。
senses.why: Once the balance is a number to be managed, verbs such as correct, improve and rebalance attach to it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦差额成为可管理的数字，纠正、改善、再平衡这类动词就会与它搭配。

senses.title: Any equilibrium between inflow and outflow
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：流入与流出之间的均衡
senses.definition: an abstract state of equilibrium between what enters and what leaves a system
senses.definitionCN: 某系统流入与流出之间达成均衡的抽象状态
senses.example: The balance of trade between the two regions shaped their politics.
senses.exampleCN: 两地区之间的进出往来格局塑造了它们的政治。
senses.why: The image of two pans can be applied to anything that flows in and out, not only to goods across a border.
senses.whyCN: 两只秤盘的意象可用于任何有进有出的事物，而不只是跨境货物。

intro.en: Balance of trade joins balance, from Latin bilanx 'two scales', with trade, a word of path and exchange. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: balance of trade 把出自拉丁 bilanx「两只有秤盘的天平」的 balance，与表示「路径与往来」的 trade 组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lanx meant a scale pan or a dish, and it named the shallow vessel on which goods were weighed.
items.cn: lanx 意为秤盘或浅盘，指称货时所用的浅器皿。

items.en: Bi- 'two' plus lanx gave bilanx, an adjective for a pair of scales, and the noun balance kept that image.
items.cn: bi-「二」加 lanx 构成 bilanx，指一对秤盘的形容词，名词 balance 保留了这一意象。

items.en: Old French balance meant both the instrument and the equality it shows, and English took it in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 balance 既指器具，也指它显示的相等，英语在 13 世纪吸收了这个词。

items.en: In the seventeenth century a favourable balance of trade meant exports exceeding imports, and the phrase became a goal of policy.
items.cn: 在 17 世纪，有利的贸易差额指出口超过进口，这个说法成为政策目标。

items.en: Modern statistical offices made the balance of trade a routine monthly figure, neutral in sign but political in use.
items.cn: 现代统计机构把贸易差额变成按月发布的常规数字，符号中性，用途却带政治性。

note.en: The first group shares the scale image or looks close to it; the second group names related accounts and measures.
note.cn: 第一组共享天平意象或与之外形相近；第二组是相关的账目与指标。

entries.definition: The beam and pans, or a state of equality; alone it can mean a bank balance or physical steadiness.
entries.definitionCN: 横梁与秤盘，或相等的状态；单独使用时也可指银行余额或身体平衡。

entries.definition: The record of all transactions with the world, including services, income and transfers; the trade balance is one part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 与世界的全部交易记录，含服务、收入与转移；贸易差额只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: A near synonym of balance of trade, used more often in headlines and tables.
entries.definitionCN: 贸易差额的近义说法，更常用于标题与表格。

entries.definition: The Latin adjective for a two-pan scale; it is the etymological root, never used in modern English trade talk.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中「双盘天平」的形容词；它是词源根，现代英语贸易语境中不用。

entries.definition: A negative balance, when imports exceed exports.
entries.definitionCN: 差额为负的情形，即进口超过出口。

entries.definition: A positive balance, when exports exceed imports.
entries.definitionCN: 差额为正的情形，即出口超过进口。

entries.definition: Exports minus imports in national accounts; it is the same quantity expressed inside a formula.
entries.definitionCN: 国民核算中出口减进口；它是同一数量在公式中的表达。

entries.definition: The balance of physical goods only, excluding services, which are called invisible trade.
entries.definitionCN: 只计实体货物的差额，不含被称为无形贸易的服务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real two-pan root, the real trade word and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「双盘」词根、真实的贸易词与真实统计搭配。

normal.en: Balance is two pans on one beam, so the phrase is simply which pan is heavier.
normal.cn: balance 是一根横梁上的两只秤盘，所以这个短语就是看哪只盘更重。

normal.en: The Latin adjective bilanx 'two-scaled' is the root, and bi- means two.
normal.cn: 拉丁形容词 bilanx「双盘的」是词根，其中 bi- 意为二。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: favourable balance, balance of trade figures, correct the balance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：有利差额、贸易差额数据、纠正差额。

normal.en: The phrase is singular and usually takes the, unlike the countable trade deficit.
normal.cn: 这个短语用单数并常带定冠词，与可数的 trade deficit 不同。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with balance of payments, which also counts services and income.
normal.cn: 不要与 balance of payments 混淆，后者还把服务与收入计入。

abstract.en: Picture two pans loaded with crates, one marked out and one marked in, and the beam settling.
abstract.cn: 想象两只秤盘装满货箱，一只标着出，一只标着进，横梁缓缓停住。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where the two columns are drawn as columns of blocks, and the taller one wins.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，两栏被画成积木柱，较高的那栏取胜。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with two counters, one clicking for arrivals and one for departures.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门有两个计数器，一个为进来的人跳，一个为出去的人跳。

examples.en: The balance of trade improved as oil imports fell.
examples.cn: 随着石油进口下降，贸易差额有所改善。

examples.en: Economists watch the balance of trade for signs of demand.
examples.cn: 经济学家观察贸易差额，以寻找需求迹象。

examples.en: A favourable balance of trade was the mercantilist ideal.
examples.cn: 出超是重商主义的理想。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「两只秤盘量进出」——balance 是天平，trade 是贸易，秤停在哪边就是贸易差额

root: balance 出自拉丁 bilanx「两只有秤盘的天平」= bi-（二）+ lanx「秤盘」，经古法语进入英语；trade 源自古英语与中古低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词。合指进出口相减后的差额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one beam: the net difference, the published account, the goods-only figure, the old favourable-unfavourable judgment, the policy signal, the period number, the object of correction and finally any inflow-outflow equilibrium.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在同一根横梁上：净差额、公布的账目、仅计货物的数字、旧式的有利不利评判、政策信号、按期发布的数字、被纠正的对象，最后是任何进出均衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans on one beam, one loaded with exports and one with imports.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根横梁上两只秤盘，一只装出口，一只装进口。

branches.en: BASE DIFFERENCE: the beam settles according to the heavier pan.
branches.cn: 基础差额：横梁按更重的那只盘停住。

branches.en: RECORD AND PERIOD: the difference is published and recalculated each period.
branches.cn: 记录与周期：差额被公布，并按期重算。

branches.en: SCOPE: the account can be narrowed to goods alone.
branches.cn: 范围：这本账可以收窄到只计货物。

branches.en: JUDGMENT AND ACTION: the balance is praised, watched or corrected.
branches.cn: 评判与行动：差额或被褒扬、被观察、被纠正。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any inflow and outflow can be weighed on the same beam.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何流入流出都能放在同一根横梁上称量。

intro.en: Balance of trade is a phrase whose core word is built from a Latin numeral and a Latin noun for a pan.
intro.cn: balance of trade 的核心词由一个拉丁数词与一个表示秤盘的名词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin bi- 'two' and lanx 'pan' give balance and bilanx; trade has a Germanic origin and gives trading, trader and trademark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 bi-「二」与 lanx「秤盘」衍生 balance 与 bilanx；trade 源自日耳曼语，衍生 trading、trader 与 trademark。

items.example: The root names the weighing dish.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指称量用的盘子。

items.example: The balance tipped to one side.

items.exampleCN: 他们达成了均衡的协议。
失衡的预算让贷款方警觉。

items.meaning: the activity of buying and selling

items.example: They publish the balance of trade monthly.
items.exampleCN: 他们每月公布贸易差额。

definition_zh: 变质岩的；变质作用的（岩石在高温高压下改变结构）；变质程度的；变质矿物的；变质带的；变态的（生物学，罕用）；发生彻底改变的（比喻）；接触变质晕的
definition_en: relating to rock that has been altered by heat and pressure, or more rarely to the biological process of changing form
core_image: 采石场的岩壁上，原来的水平层理被压成波状褶皱，云母片在光下闪出一层银亮
scene: 采石场的岩壁上，原来的层理被压成波状褶皱。 In the quarry wall, metamorphic rock has been folded until the old bedding waves.
sceneCN: 这里 metamorphic 指「经高温高压而改变结构与矿物组成的岩石」（第 1 个义项：变质岩的）；句意为采石场岩壁上的变质岩被压成波状褶皱，原有层理不再平直。可辨识物件：波状层理、云母闪光、采石场岩壁、褶皱。

pos.zh: 变质岩的；变质作用的；变态的（罕用）；彻底改变的

senses.title: Rock altered by heat and pressure
senses.titleCN: 经高温高压改变的岩石
senses.definition: describing rock whose minerals and texture have been changed by heat, pressure or hot fluids
senses.definitionCN: 矿物与结构因热、压力或热液而改变的岩石
senses.example: In the quarry wall, metamorphic rock has been folded until the old bedding waves.
senses.exampleCN: 采石场岩壁上的变质岩被压成波状褶皱，原有层理不再平直。
senses.why: The adjective marks a origin: the rock was once something else, and heat or pressure rewrote its minerals.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出来历：岩石原本是别的东西，热或压力改写了它的矿物。

senses.title: The process of alteration
senses.definition: relating to the process by which such change occurs, as in metamorphic processes at depth
senses.definitionCN: 与这种改变发生的过程有关，如深部的变质过程
senses.example: Metamorphic processes at depth recrystallise limestone into marble.
senses.exampleCN: 深部的变质过程把石灰岩重结晶为大理岩。
senses.why: Here the adjective attaches to the process rather than the product, a distinction geologists keep carefully.
senses.whyCN: 此处形容词附于过程而非产物，地质学家严格区分这两者。

senses.title: A grade or intensity of change
senses.definition: describing the level of alteration, from low grade to high grade, as shown by index minerals
senses.definitionCN: 描述改变的等级，从低级到高级，由指示矿物显示
senses.example: The metamorphic grade rises toward the granite contact.
senses.exampleCN: 越靠近花岗岩接触带，变质程度越高。
senses.why: Grade turns the adjective into a scale, so one rock can be more metamorphic than another.
senses.whyCN: 程度把这个形容词变成一把标尺，因此一块岩石可以比另一块更变质。

senses.title: Minerals produced by alteration
senses.definition: describing minerals that grow during alteration, such as garnet, staurolite or kyanite
senses.definitionCN: 在变质过程中生长的矿物，如石榴石、十字石或蓝晶石
senses.example: Garnet is a metamorphic mineral in this schist.
senses.exampleCN: 石榴石是这片片岩中的变质矿物。
senses.why: Index minerals let geologists read temperature and pressure from a hand sample.
senses.whyCN: 指示矿物让地质学家能从一块手标本读出温度与压力。

senses.title: A belt or zone of altered rock
senses.definition: describing a mapped region where rocks share a history of alteration, as in a metamorphic belt
senses.definitionCN: 描述一片岩石共享变质历史的填图区域，如变质带
senses.example: The metamorphic belt runs along the old continental edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这条变质带沿古老的陆缘延伸。
senses.why: Mapping turns the adjective into a spatial label, which is how regional geology is organized.
senses.whyCN: 填图把这个形容词变成空间标签，区域地质即以此组织。

senses.title: The contact aureole
senses.definition: describing the zone around an intrusion where heat altered the surrounding rock
senses.definitionCN: 描述侵入体周围受热改变的那一圈围岩
senses.example: The metamorphic aureole around the granite is only a few metres wide.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩周围的接触变质晕只有几米宽。
senses.why: The aureole records a local heat source, so the adjective points to a cause as well as a result.
senses.whyCN: 变质晕记录了局部的热源，形容词因此既指结果也指原因。

senses.title: Biological change of form
senses.definition: a rare biological use meaning 'of or showing metamorphosis', mostly replaced by the noun and verb
senses.definitionCN: 罕见的生物学用法，意为「变态的」，多被名词与动词取代
senses.example: Older texts call the pupal stage a metamorphic phase.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的文献把蛹期称为变态阶段。
senses.why: Geology took over the adjective, so the biological sense survives mostly in older writing.
senses.whyCN: 地质学占用了这个形容词，生物义因此主要残存在较早的写作中。

senses.title: Thoroughly transformed
senses.definition: used figuratively for something changed so deeply that its earlier state is hard to recognize
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指被改变得极深、以致早期状态难以辨认的事物
senses.example: The metamorphic economy of the town no longer resembles its mining past.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小镇蜕变后的经济已看不出采矿业时期的模样。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the geologists' idea of a rock rewritten from within, not merely repainted.
senses.whyCN: 比喻借用地质学家「岩石从内部被改写」的想法，而非仅仅重新刷漆。

intro.en: Metamorphic is meta- 'change' plus morphē 'form' plus -ic 'relating to', the adjective partner of metamorphosis. Geology adopted it in the nineteenth century for altered rock.
intro.cn: metamorphic 是 meta-「改变」加 morphē「形态」再加 -ic「与……有关的」，是 metamorphosis 的形容词伙伴。地质学在 19 世纪把它用于变质岩。

items.en: Meta- meant 'change, beyond' and morphē meant 'form'; the two already combined in Greek to name transformation.
items.cn: meta- 意为「改变、超越」，morphē 意为「形态」；两者在希腊语中已组合表示变形。

items.en: The suffix -ic, from Greek -ikos, means 'relating to', so metamorphic says 'pertaining to a change of form'.
items.cn: -ic 后缀出自希腊 -ikos，意为「与……有关」，因此 metamorphic 表示「与形态改变有关的」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology needed a word for rock whose minerals had been recrystallised, and metamorphic filled the gap alongside metamorphism.
items.cn: 19 世纪地质学需要一个词来描述矿物已重结晶的岩石，metamorphic 与 metamorphism 一同补上这个空缺。

items.en: The adjective became standard in phrases such as metamorphic rock, metamorphic grade and metamorphic facies, which now dominate all usage.
items.cn: 这个形容词在「metamorphic rock」「metamorphic grade」「metamorphic facies」等短语中成为标准，如今主导全部用法。

items.en: The older biological sense survives in a few phrases such as metamorphic phase, but the noun and verb carry that meaning today.
items.cn: 较早的生物义残存在「metamorphic phase」这类短语里，今天该意义由名词与动词承担。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and attribution): the exact first geological use and the writer who fixed the term are not settled, so no single citation should be treated as definitive.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与归属）：最早的地质学用法与确立该术语的作者均无定论，不应把某一条书证当作定论。

note.en: Group one separates metamorphic from the noun, verb and similar-looking words; group two lists the rock-class words it is contrasted with.
note.cn: 第一组把 metamorphic 与名词、动词及形近词分开；第二组列出与它对照的岩石分类词。

entries.definition: Metamorphosis is the process; metamorphic describes what the process produced.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphosis 是过程；metamorphic 描述该过程的产物。

entries.definition: Metamorphose is the action, so it cannot replace the adjective before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphose 是动作，不能替代名词前的形容词。

entries.definition: Metamorphism names the geological process, a narrower noun than metamorphosis.
entries.definitionCN: metamorphism 指地质过程，是比 metamorphosis 更窄的名词。

entries.definition: Metaphoric comes from metaphor and Greek pherein 'to carry', so it is not related to form at all.
entries.definitionCN: metaphoric 出自 metaphor 与希腊 pherein「携带」，与形态无关。

entries.definition: Igneous rock solidified from melt, so heat made it but did not alter an earlier rock.
entries.definitionCN: igneous 指由熔体凝固的岩石，热产生了它，却没有改造先前的岩石。

entries.definition: Sedimentary rock formed from deposited material; metamorphic rock may have started as sediment and been rewritten.
entries.definitionCN: sedimentary 由沉积物形成；变质岩可能原本就是沉积物，之后被改写。

entries.definition: Recrystallised describes the mineral change itself, the mechanism behind a metamorphic texture.
entries.definitionCN: recrystallised 描述矿物改变本身，是变质结构背后的机制。

entries.definition: Altered is the general word for any change and lacks the specific pressure-and-heat meaning.
entries.definitionCN: altered 是泛指改变，不含特定的高温高压义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Meta- 'change' plus morph- 'form' plus -ic 'relating to' gives the meaning directly.
normal.cn: meta-「改变」加 morph-「形态」加 -ic「与……有关」，意义直接可得。

normal.en: The family runs metamorphosis, metamorphose, metamorphic and metamorphism.
normal.cn: 词族包括 metamorphosis、metamorphose、metamorphic 与 metamorphism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: metamorphic rock, metamorphic grade, metamorphic facies.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：变质岩、变质程度、变质相。

normal.en: The three rock classes are igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.
normal.cn: 三大岩石类别是岩浆岩、沉积岩与变质岩。

normal.en: A metamorphic rock was something else first; that is the whole point of the word.
normal.cn: 变质岩原本是别的东西，这正是这个词的全部要点。

abstract.en: Picture a limestone bed squeezed until its grains lock into a new mosaic.
abstract.cn: 想象一层石灰岩被挤压，直到颗粒嵌成新的镶嵌。

abstract.en: Picture a letter rewritten so often that only the handwriting is the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被反复改写，只剩笔迹还是原来的。

abstract.en: Picture a town whose mine closes and whose streets fill with studios.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇矿井关闭，街道上开满了工作室。

examples.en: Metamorphic rock around the intrusion contains garnet and staurolite.
examples.cn: 侵入体周围的变质岩含石榴石与十字石。

examples.en: The map divides the region into three metamorphic belts.
examples.cn: 地图把该地区划分为三条变质带。

examples.en: Marble is metamorphic limestone, recrystallised under pressure.
examples.cn: 大理岩是受压重结晶的变质石灰岩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「meta（变）+ morph（形）+ ic」——形态被改过的 → 变质岩的

root: 希腊 meta-「改变」+ morphē「形态」+ -ic「与……有关的」，是 metamorphosis 的形容词形式。19 世纪地质学采用为「变质岩的」。最早地质学用法与确立者无定论，属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take the adjective through altered rock, the altering process, its grade, its index minerals, its mapped belts, its contact aureole, a rare biological use and a general metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让这个形容词经过变质岩、变质过程、变质程度、指示矿物、填图变质带、接触变质晕、罕见的生物义与一般比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a once-flat limestone bed folded into waves, its grains grown into a new sparkling mosaic.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层原本平整的石灰岩被压成波状，颗粒长成新的闪光镶嵌。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: rock that was something else before.
branches.cn: 产物：此前是别的东西的岩石。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: heat, pressure and fluids do the rewriting.
branches.cn: 过程：热、压力与流体完成改写。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: grade and index minerals turn the adjective into a thermometer.
branches.cn: 度量：变质程度与指示矿物把形容词变成温度计。

branches.en: SPACE: belts map the history and aureoles mark a local heat source.
branches.cn: 空间：变质带勾勒历史，变质晕标出局部热源。

branches.en: OUTSIDE GEOLOGY: a rare biological use and a metaphor for deep change.
branches.cn: 地质学之外：罕见的生物义与深层改变的比喻。

intro.en: Metamorphic is built from Greek meta-, morphē and the suffix -ic; the same elements form metamorphosis, metamorphism and many technical compounds.
intro.cn: metamorphic 由希腊 meta-、morphē 与后缀 -ic 构成；同一批成分也构成 metamorphosis、metamorphism 与许多技术复合词。

latinIntro.en: Greek meta- and morphē give metamorphosis, metamorphic, metamorphism and amorphous; -ic marks the relational adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 meta- 与 morphē 构成 metamorphosis、metamorphic、metamorphism 与 amorphous；-ic 标出关系形容词。

items.example: The root names what is altered.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指明被改变的东西。
这里的变质岩发生褶皱。
变质沉积层仍显示层理。
谷底之下是变质火山岩。
视物变形症让直线变弯。

definition_zh: v. （为小事）争吵不休；潺潺作响
definition_en: to argue about small unimportant things; of a stream, to flow with a soft babbling sound
core_image: 两个人隔着一张餐桌，为谁该洗碗你来我往地顶嘴
scene: 两兄弟为了电视遥控器吵了一整晚。 The two brothers bickered over the television remote all evening.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bicker 指为琐事持续不断地拌嘴；句意是两兄弟为电视遥控器吵了一整晚。

pos.zh: 拌嘴；争吵不休

senses.title: To quarrel about trifles
senses.definition: to argue repeatedly about small matters that do not really matter
senses.definitionCN: 为并不重要的小事反复争吵
senses.example: The couple bickered about the route until they missed the turn.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻为路线争吵不休，结果错过了转弯。
senses.why: The word began as a name for a small skirmish, so it keeps the idea of a fight that is not a war.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指小规模交锋，因此始终带着「不是战争的打斗」之意。

senses.title: Of a stream, to babble
senses.definition: to make the light running sound of water over stones
senses.definitionCN: 水流过石头时发出的细碎声响
senses.example: A stream bickered under the wooden bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小溪在木桥下潺潺作响。
senses.why: A small stream sounds like two people trading words, so the quarrel sense was lent to water.
senses.whyCN: 小溪的声音像两个人你来我往地顶嘴，于是「争吵」义借给了流水。

intro.en: Bicker is of uncertain origin; it first names a small skirmish, then a petty quarrel, and later the sound of running water.
intro.cn: bicker 词源不确定；它先指小规模交锋，再指琐碎争吵，后来也指流水的声音。

items.en: Middle English bikeren means to attack or skirmish.
items.cn: 中古英语 bikeren 意为攻击、小规模交锋。

items.en: The earliest recorded use is a clash, not a quarrel.
items.cn: 最早记载的用法是冲突，而不是口角。

items.en: The word shifts from blows to words exchanged over trifles.
items.cn: 这个词由动手转为琐事上的你来我往。

items.en: The modern pattern of constant small quarrelling settles in.
items.cn: 「持续的小争吵」这一现代用法固定下来。

items.en: Writers borrow the word for water running over stones.
items.cn: 作家把这词借去形容水过石头的声音。

items.en: Bicker now almost always means a low-level, ongoing dispute.
items.cn: 现代 bicker 几乎总指低烈度、持续不断的争执。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes with bicker; the near-meaning group arranges the words from a running low quarrel to a formal dispute.
note.cn: 形近组与 bicker 押韵；近义组由低烈度的持续口角排到正式的争辩。

entries.definition: To shine with an unsteady light.
entries.definitionCN: 光忽明忽暗地闪。

entries.definition: To laugh in a suppressed, mocking way.
entries.definitionCN: 窃笑；暗笑。

entries.definition: A device that makes a regular ticking sound.
entries.definitionCN: 发滴答声的装置。

entries.definition: A person or thing that kicks.
entries.definitionCN: 踢的人或物。

entries.definition: To quarrel noisily about something trivial.
entries.definitionCN: 为琐事大声争吵。

entries.definition: To have an angry disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒地争执。

entries.definition: To argue at length and crossly.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间地激烈争辩。

entries.definition: To give reasons for and against something.
entries.definitionCN: 提出正反理由。

normalIntro.en: Bicker sounds like two chickens pecking at each other over a grain of corn.
normalIntro.cn: bicker 听起来像两只鸡为一粒玉米互相啄来啄去。

normal.en: Say bicker quickly and you hear a small, repeated snap.
normal.cn: 快念 bicker，能听见细碎而不断的一下一下。

normal.en: It began as a skirmish, a fight too small to call a battle.
normal.cn: 它原指一场小到称不上战役的交锋。

normal.en: Bicker is a quarrel with no winner and no end.
normal.cn: bicker 是一场没有胜负也没有尽头的争吵。

normal.en: The same small snapping sound belongs to a stream.
normal.cn: 同样的细碎断续声也属于一条小溪。

normal.en: If nobody will remember the issue tomorrow, it is a bicker.
normal.cn: 如果明天没人记得争的是什么，那就是 bicker。

abstract.en: Two keys tapping the same small argument.
abstract.cn: 两把钥匙反复敲同一个不值一提的争论。

abstract.en: A duel fought with teaspoons.
abstract.cn: 用茶匙进行的决斗。

abstract.en: Noise that never turns into a decision.
abstract.cn: 始终无法变成决定的声音。

examples.en: They bickered about whose turn it was to pay.
examples.cn: 他们为轮到谁付钱而拌嘴。

examples.en: The neighbours bicker over the parking space every week.
examples.cn: 邻居每周都为车位争吵。

examples.en: A small brook bickered beneath the planks.
examples.cn: 一条小溪在木板桥下潺潺作响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必磕」——为一点小事一定要磕到底，谁也不让谁。

root: 中古英语 bikeren（小规模交锋），词源不确定，可能为拟声

sensesIntro.en: The quarrel sense and the water sense share one sound: a small, fast, repeated tapping that never quite stops.
sensesIntro.cn: 争吵义与流水义共有一个声音：细碎、快速、反复不停。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people leaning across a table, each holding one end of the same argument
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔桌而倾，各执同一场争论的一端

branches.en: A remote control between two hands.
branches.cn: 两只手之间的一个遥控器。

branches.en: Dishes left in the sink again.
branches.cn: 又留在水池里的碗碟。

branches.en: Water slipping over pebbles.
branches.cn: 滑过卵石的水。

branches.en: A sound heard under a footbridge.
branches.cn: 桥下听见的声音。

branches.en: Small repeated noise with no conclusion.
branches.cn: 反复的小声音，没有结论。

intro.en: Bicker has an uncertain stem but takes regular English endings; the list below builds its forms and the vocabulary of quarrels.
intro.cn: bicker 词干来源不确定，但配的是规则英语词尾；下面列出它的各种形式与「争吵」词场的词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin altercari means to bandy words, iurgare to wrangle, and rixari to brawl.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altercari 意为你来我往地争辩，iurgare 意为争吵，rixari 意为斗殴。

latinEntries.exampleCN: iurgare 是 objurgate 的来源。

definition_zh: 附录；补遗；补充条款
definition_en: an extra item, note, or section added to a book, document, or agreement
core_image: 合同签完又多钉进去一页补充
scene: 合同双方都签了字，律师忽然想起漏了一条免责条款，当场多拟了一页订在后面。 The lawyer drafted an addendum to cover the missing clause.
sceneCN: 这里 addendum 是「附录、补充条款」（第 1 个义项：加在文件后面补充内容的部分）；句意为律师草拟了一份附录补上遗漏的条款。

pos.zh: 附录；补遗；补充条款

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「加法；增加物」

senses.title: A section added to a document
senses.definition: a part added after a document is finished, to supply something missing or new
senses.definitionCN: 文件完成后追加的部分，用以补充遗漏或新增内容
senses.example: The lawyer drafted an addendum to cover the missing clause.
senses.exampleCN: 律师草拟了一份附录补上遗漏的条款。
senses.why: Latin dare means 'to give'; an addendum is what is given to the text after the text is done.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dare 意为「给予」；addendum 就是文本完成后被「补给」文本的东西。

senses.title: A late addition to a book
senses.definition: a note or correction appended to a published book
senses.definitionCN: 附在已出版书籍末尾的说明或更正
senses.example: The second printing carries an addendum correcting two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次印刷附了一份更正两个年份的补遗。
senses.why: What was discovered too late to enter the main text is given its own little tail page.
senses.whyCN: 来不及进入正文的发现，被「补给」了自己的一页小尾巴。

intro.en: Addendum is the Latin gerundive of addere, 'to be added', from ad- 'to' plus dare 'to give'.
intro.cn: addendum 是拉丁语 addere（增添）的动形词，意为「应被加上之物」，由 ad-（向）加 dare（给予）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *do- meant 'to give'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *do- 意为「给予」。

items.en: dare meant 'to give'; addere meant 'to give to, to add'.
items.cn: dare 意为「给予」；addere 意为「加给、增添」。

items.en: addendum was the gerundive: 'the thing that must be added'.
items.cn: addendum 是动形词：「必须被加上之物」。

items.en: English borrowed the word for appended matter in books.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指书末附加的内容。

items.en: Now common in contracts as well as books; plural addenda survives in formal use.
items.cn: 如今合同与书籍都用；正式场合保留拉丁式复数 addenda。

note.en: The first group gathers the dare family of adding words; the second gathers words for appended material.
note.cn: 第一组收 dare 词族的「添加」词；第二组收表示附加内容的词。

entries.definition: The Latin-style plural of addendum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，addendum 的拉丁式复数。

entries.definition: The act or result of adding; a longer-lived cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加法；增加物」，同根近亲。

entries.definition: To cite as evidence; only the first letters overlap, root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引证」；仅开头拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A body of extra material at the end of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附录」，常指书末整块附加材料。

entries.definition: A section or building added to something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附件；附属建筑」。

entries.definition: Something added to complete or extend a work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充；增刊」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the dare root and the contract scene; the abstract hooks picture an extra page pinned at the end.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 dare 词根与合同场景；抽象记忆点想象末尾多钉一页。

normal.en: Addendum is 'the thing to be added': ad- plus dare.
normal.cn: addendum 意为「应加之物」：ad- 加 dare。

normal.en: The formal plural is addenda.
normal.cn: 正式复数是 addenda。

normal.en: Contract addendum is common in legal English.
normal.cn: contract addendum 在法律英语中常见。

normal.en: An addendum comes after the main text is done.
normal.cn: addendum 出现在正文完成之后。

normal.en: It shares the root with add and addition.
normal.cn: 它与 add 和 addition 同根。

abstract.en: Picture a page slipped in and stapled after signatures.
abstract.cn: 想象签字后又订进去的一页纸。

abstract.en: Picture a book growing a small extra tail.
abstract.cn: 想象书长出一条小尾巴。

abstract.en: Picture a hand adding one last brick to a finished wall.
abstract.cn: 想象往完工的墙上补最后一块砖。

examples.en: The lawyer drafted an addendum to cover the missing clause.
examples.cn: 律师草拟了一份附录补上遗漏的条款。

examples.en: Please review the addenda before signing the agreement.
examples.cn: 签署协议前请先审阅各份补充条款。

examples.en: The second printing carries an addendum correcting two dates.
examples.cn: 第二次印刷附了一份更正两个年份的补遗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额顶达姆」——合同额头上多顶出一页补丁，就是附录。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ dare（给予）→ addere（增添）→ addendum（应加之物）；核心义是「事后补送给文本的东西」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from appended contract matter, to late corrections in a book.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从合同的追加条款，走到书籍的迟来补正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an extra page pinned after the last page
core.cn: 核心意象：末页之后多钉的一页

branches.en: The extra clause that completes a contract.
branches.cn: 补全合同的追加条款。

branches.en: The late note that mends a published book.
branches.cn: 修补已出版书籍的迟来说明。

branches.en: Both senses arrive after the work is finished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出现在工作完成之后。

branches.en: Legal English keeps this sense busy.
branches.cn: 法律英语频繁使用这个义项。

branches.en: Both rest on the Latin idea of 'giving to'.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「加给」的观念。

intro.en: The word joins the prefix ad- with the give-root dend-, and the family spreads through add, addition, and date-related words.
intro.cn: 这个词把前缀 ad- 与「给」词根 dend- 结合，词族遍布 add、addition 及与日期相关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin addere and its gerundive addendum are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 addere 及其动形词 addendum。

latinEntries.meaning: the thing that must be added

definition_zh: 动物行为学；行为学：在自然条件下系统研究动物行为的学科；（早期义）性格描写、模仿表演
definition_en: the scientific study of animal behavior, especially in natural conditions, and historically the art of portraying character
core_image: 黎明前，一个裹在伪装帐里的人一动不动地坐着，只用铅笔记录一只鸟每一次转身的先后顺序
scene: 天亮以前，观察者躲在伪装帐里记下每只鸟求偶动作的先后次序，完全不改变周围的条件。 Before dawn the observer sits in a blind and writes down the order of each bird's display, altering nothing in the habitat, which is the method that defines ethology.
sceneCN: 这里 ethology 指「在自然条件下系统观察动物行为的学科」（第 1 个义项：动物行为学）；句意为观察者在伪装帐中按顺序记下求偶动作、不改变环境，这正是该学科的方法。可辨识物件：伪装帐、望远镜、铅笔、正在展示的鸟。

pos.zh: 动物行为学；行为学（学科名，不可数）
（早期用法）性格描写；以模仿刻画性格的表演

collocations.zh: 动物行为学与比较心理学

forms.label: 复数（罕见，指多种行为学研究）

derivatives.zh: 动物行为学的；行为学意义上的

senses.title: The study of animal behavior
senses.titleCN: 动物行为学：在自然条件下研究动物行为的学科
senses.definition: the branch of zoology that studies behavior, especially as observed in natural conditions
senses.definitionCN: 动物学的分支，研究行为，尤其侧重自然条件下的观察
senses.example: Ethology began with long hours of watching animals that were not disturbed.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学始于长时间观察不被打扰的动物。
senses.why: The Greek root ēthos means character or habitual disposition, so the name promises an account of how an animal characteristically conducts itself.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 ēthos 意为性格或习惯性情，因此这个名字承诺给出动物典型行事的说明。

senses.title: The comparative tradition
senses.definition: the tradition that compares behavior across species in order to reconstruct its evolution
senses.definitionCN: 跨物种比较行为、以重建其进化的研究传统
senses.example: The classic ethology of the 1930s compared displays across bird families.
senses.exampleCN: 20 世纪 30 年代的经典行为学比较了不同鸟科的表现。
senses.why: If character is species-specific, it can be compared between species, and comparison was the method that gave the field its identity.
senses.whyCN: 如果性格因物种而异，就能在物种间比较；比较正是赋予这门学科身份的方法。

senses.title: Historical sense: character portrayal
senses.titleCN: 早期义：性格描写与模仿表演
senses.definition: the older, seventeenth-century sense of depicting character by mimicry or description
senses.definitionCN: 17 世纪较早的义项：以模仿或描写刻画性格
senses.example: In the older sense, ethology belonged to the stage rather than to zoology.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的义项里，ethology 属于舞台而非动物学。
senses.why: The word entered English through Latin ethologia, a borrowing of Greek ēthologia 'character portrayal', long before it named a science.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经拉丁 ethologia 进入英语，那是希腊 ēthologia「性格刻画」的借词，远早于它成为科学名称。

senses.title: Study of instinct and fixed patterns
senses.titleCN: 对本能与固定动作模式的研究
senses.definition: the study of unlearned, stereotyped patterns and the signals that release them
senses.definitionCN: 对非学习的刻板模式及其释放信号的研究
senses.example: Ethology gave fixed action patterns their name and their evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学为固定动作模式提供了名称与证据。
senses.why: The early ethologists needed behaviour that could be recognised across individuals, and unlearned patterns supplied exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 早期行为学家需要可在个体间辨认的行为，而非学习的刻板模式恰好提供这一点。

senses.title: Contrast with laboratory psychology
senses.titleCN: 与实验室心理学的对照
senses.definition: the field defined by natural observation as against controlled indoor experiment
senses.definitionCN: 以自然观察为标志、与室内受控实验相对的领域
senses.example: Ethology trusts the field notebook; experimental psychology trusts the lever and the timer.
senses.exampleCN: 动物行为学信任野外记录本；实验心理学信任杠杆与计时器。
senses.why: Two ways of knowing the same animal grew side by side, and the name ethology marked the one that insists on the habitat.
senses.whyCN: 认识同一动物的两条道路并肩生长，ethology 这个名字标出了坚持栖息地的那一条。

senses.title: Method: field observation and individual recognition
senses.titleCN: 方法：野外观察与个体识别
senses.definition: the practice of identifying individuals and recording sequences without intervening
senses.definitionCN: 辨认个体并在不介入的情况下记录行为序列的做法
senses.example: The ethology of the troop depended on knowing every face.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体的行为学依赖对每一张面孔的识别。
senses.why: A sequence is only evidence if the same individual is followed, so the method had to invent ways of telling animals apart.
senses.whyCN: 只有当同一个体被持续跟踪，序列才算证据，因此这套方法必须发明辨认动物的手段。

senses.title: Modern extension: cognition and welfare
senses.titleCN: 现代扩展：认知与动物福利
senses.definition: the contemporary extension of the field to animal cognition, emotion and welfare
senses.definitionCN: 该领域向动物认知、情绪与福利的当代扩展
senses.example: Modern ethology tests whether a captive animal can choose its own routine.
senses.exampleCN: 现代动物行为学检验圈养动物能否选择自己的日常安排。
senses.why: Once natural conduct is the standard, confinement can be judged by how much of that conduct it allows.
senses.whyCN: 一旦自然举止成为标准，圈养就能按它允许多少这类举止来评判。

senses.title: Abstract: systematic account of a disposition
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：对某种习性的系统描述
senses.definition: any systematic description of the characteristic conduct of a group or type
senses.definitionCN: 对某一群体或类型的典型举止所作的任何系统描述
senses.example: The novelist offers an ethology of the office, not of animals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家写的是一门办公室行为学，而非动物行为学。
senses.why: Because ēthos means character, the word can always be borrowed back from zoology to mean an account of how a kind of creature lives.
senses.whyCN: 因为 ēthos 意为性格，这个词总能从动物学借回来，指对某一类存在者生活方式的说明。

intro.en: Ethology comes from Latin ethologia, a borrowing of Greek ēthologia 'character portrayal', built on ēthos 'character, habit' plus -logia 'study, account'. Its zoological sense is a nineteenth-century narrowing.
intro.cn: ethology 来自拉丁 ethologia，那是希腊 ēthologia「性格刻画」的借词，由 ēthos「性格、习惯」加 -logia「研究、叙述」构成。其动物学义是 19 世纪的收窄。

items.en: Ēthos meant 'habitual character and disposition, moral character, custom'. Its deeper origin is debated; it is often connected with the reflexive pronoun root *s(w)e-, but that link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: ēthos 意为「习惯性的性格与性情、道德品格、习俗」。其更深来源有争论，常被联系到反身代词词根 *s(w)e-，但该联系属重构。

items.en: Ēthologia meant 'character portrayal', the art of depicting a person's disposition, with no reference to animals.
items.cn: ēthologia 意为「性格刻画」，即描绘一个人性情的技艺，与动物无关。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as ethologia, and it is this Latin form that passed into English.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊词借作 ethologia，正是这个拉丁形式传入了英语。

items.en: English ethology is recorded from the late seventeenth century meaning 'mimicry, the art of depicting character by gesture'.
items.cn: 英语 ethology 自 17 世纪晚期有记录，义为「模仿，以手势刻画性格的技艺」。

items.en: Mill used it in 1843 for the science of character formation, and by 1897 it named the zoological study of animal behavior.
items.cn: 密尔在 1843 年用它指性格形成的科学；到 1897 年，它已指动物行为的动物学研究。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of ēthos is not established, and the claim that it shares a root with ethics rests on the same reconstructed base, so both should be labelled reconstruction rather than fact.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ēthos 在希腊语之前的历史未获确证；说它与伦理学同根，依据的是同一个重构词基，因此两者都应标为重构而非事实。

note.en: Group one separates forms built on the same Greek root from a look-alike built on a different one; group two holds fields that study the same animals with other methods.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一希腊词根构成的形式与另一词根构成的形近词；第二组是用别的方法研究同样动物的领域。

entries.definition: The adjective from ethology, meaning 'of the study of animal behavior'.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ethology 构成的形容词，意为「动物行为学的」。

entries.definition: A person who practises ethology; the -ist suffix names the worker, not the field.
entries.definitionCN: 从事动物行为学的人；-ist 后缀命名从业者，而非学科。

entries.definition: From Greek ēthikos 'of character', built on the same ēthos; it concerns moral conduct, not animal observation.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 ēthikos「关于性格的」，建立在同一个 ēthos 上；它关乎道德行为，而非动物观察。

entries.definition: From Greek ethnos 'people' plus -logia: the comparative study of peoples, not of animal character.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 ethnos「族群」加 -logia：对各民族的比较研究，而非动物性格。

entries.definition: The study of behavior as an answer to ecological conditions; ethology is older and more descriptive.
entries.definitionCN: 把行为当作对生态条件的回答来研究；ethology 更早、更偏描述。

entries.definition: The study of animal behavior by controlled experiment and cross-species comparison, often in laboratories.
entries.definitionCN: 通过受控实验与跨物种比较研究动物行为，常在实验室进行。

entries.definition: The study of the biological basis of social behavior, especially through inclusive fitness.
entries.definitionCN: 研究社会行为的生物学基础，尤其通过广义适合度。

entries.definition: A school explaining behavior by stimulus and response; it shares the word 'behavior' but not the field method.
entries.definitionCN: 以刺激—反应解释行为的学派；共用 behavior 一词，但不共用领域方法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ēthos 'character' + -logia 'study': the study of how a creature characteristically lives.
normal.cn: ēthos「性格」+ -logia「研究」：研究一种生物如何按其性格生活。

normal.en: The family runs ethology, ethological, ethologically, ethologist, ethogram.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ethology、ethological、ethologically、ethologist、ethogram。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: field ethology, the rise of ethology, a classic of ethology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：野外行为学、行为学的兴起、行为学经典著作。

normal.en: Ethics shares the Greek root ēthos but concerns moral conduct.
normal.cn: 伦理学共用希腊词根 ēthos，但关乎道德行为。

normal.en: The classic method is the blind, the notebook and the identified individual.
normal.cn: 经典方法是伪装帐、记录本与已识别的个体。

abstract.en: Picture a watcher who becomes furniture so the animals forget the watcher.
abstract.cn: 想象观察者变成家具，让动物忘了他。

abstract.en: Picture a species' whole temperament written out as a list of ordered acts.
abstract.cn: 想象把一个物种的全部性情写成一张按序排列的动作清单。

abstract.en: Picture the same word borrowed back to describe the habits of an office.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词被借回来描述一间办公室的习气。

examples.en: Ethology insists that behavior be described before it is explained.
examples.cn: 动物行为学坚持先描述行为，再解释行为。

examples.en: Her fieldwork became a classic of ethology.
examples.cn: 她的野外工作成了行为学经典。

examples.en: The old sense of ethology survives in essays on stage mimicry.
examples.cn: ethology 的旧义仍残存在论舞台模仿的文章里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「etho（性格/习性）+ logy（学）」——研究动物天生习性的一门学问 → 动物行为学

root: 希腊 ēthologia「性格刻画」= ēthos（性格、习惯）+ -logia（研究、叙述）；经拉丁 ethologia 进入英语，动物学义为 19 世纪收窄；希腊语之前的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one word from a stage art, through a nineteenth-century science of character, into field observation, then out again into cognition, welfare and any account of a characteristic way of living.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项追踪同一个词：从舞台技艺，到 19 世纪的性格科学，进入野外观察，再扩展至认知、福利，最后到任何关于典型生活方式的描述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unobtrusive watcher writing down the order of what an animal does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个不引人注意的观察者，记下动物动作的先后顺序。

branches.en: WATCHING WELL: the discipline and the method that identifies individuals and keeps hands off.
branches.cn: 好好观察：学科本身，以及辨认个体、不加干预的方法。

branches.en: PATTERNS COMPARED: species are set beside species, and unlearned patterns give the comparison solid units.
branches.cn: 被比较的模式：物种与物种并置，非学习的模式为比较提供坚实单位。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: character portrayal, still visible when the word is borrowed back.
branches.cn: 旧义：性格刻画，当这个词被借回时仍可见。

branches.en: TWO WAYS OF KNOWING: the field notebook against the lever and the timer.
branches.cn: 两种认识方式：野外记录本对杠杆与计时器。

branches.en: FROM ANIMALS TO ANY CHARACTER: welfare today, and any systematic account of a disposition at the widest.
branches.cn: 从动物到任何性格：今日的福利研究，以及在最宽处对任何性情的系统描述。

intro.en: Ethology is a Greek compound that reached English through Latin, so each of its pieces has a clear history even though the word looks opaque.
intro.cn: ethology 是一个经拉丁语传入英语的希腊复合词，因此尽管词形看似难解，每个部分都有清楚的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributed the borrowed form ethologia, but no Latin root; the pieces are Greek ēthos and -logia. Since there is no Latin cognate family, no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了借词形式 ethologia，但未贡献词根；两个部分都是希腊语 ēthos 与 -logia。由于没有拉丁同族词族，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The first element names what is portrayed or studied.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分命名被刻画或研究的对象。

items.example: Biology and ethnology use the same suffix.
items.exampleCN: biology 与 ethnology 使用同一后缀。

items.meaning: the study of animal character and behavior
items.meaningCN: 研究动物性格与行为的学科
items.example: Ethology grew out of natural history.
items.exampleCN: ethology 从博物学中生长出来。

items.example: The ethological literature is full of sequence diagrams.
items.exampleCN: 行为学文献里满是序列图。

items.meaning: from an ethological point of view
items.example: Ethologically, the two calls are distinct.
items.exampleCN: 从行为学上看，这两种叫声不同。

items.example: The ethologist spent a year in the canopy.
items.exampleCN: 这位行为学家在树冠层待了一年。

items.example: The ethogram lists forty distinct acts.
items.exampleCN: 行为谱列出四十种不同的动作。

items.meaning: the character of a people or group
items.meaningCN: 群体或民族的精神气质
items.example: The ethos of the group shaped its gestures.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体的气质塑造了它的手势。

items.example: Ethnology is a different field built on a different root.
items.exampleCN: ethnology 是建立在另一个词根上的不同领域。

definition_zh: 下流的；猥亵的；淫秽打诨的
definition_en: dealing with sexual matters in a comically crude way
core_image: 酒馆里哄笑的荤段子
scene: 老酒馆中水手们拍着桌子大笑，讲着不登大雅之堂的笑话。 Sailors roared at a bawdy song.
sceneCN: 这里 bawdy 指「下流打诨的」（第 1 个义项：以粗俗方式谈性）；句意：水手们对着一支荤歌哄堂大笑。

pos.zh: 下流的；猥亵的

senses.title: Coarsely humorous about sex
senses.definition: dealing with sex in a funny, crude way
senses.definitionCN: 以逗笑的粗俗方式谈论性事
senses.example: The roast included some bawdy jokes.
senses.exampleCN: 那场吐槽大会里有几个荤段子。
senses.why: From the bawd, who ran the sex trade; her trade colors her speech.
senses.whyCN: 出自老鸨 bawd——操皮肉生意者；其行当染其言语。

senses.title: Indecent language or songs
senses.definition: obscene in speech or song
senses.definitionCN: 言语或歌曲中猥亵
senses.example: Soldiers sang bawdy songs around the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们围着篝火唱下流小调。
senses.why: The trade's talk became a genre of fun.
senses.whyCN: 皮肉行业的谈吐成了一种玩笑文体。

senses.title: The noun bawd
senses.definition: a person who manages prostitutes; a procurer
senses.definitionCN: 管理娼妓之人；拉皮条者
senses.example: The play's bawd greets every customer.
senses.exampleCN: 戏中的鸨母迎来送往。
senses.why: The root person-word precedes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 表人的词根先于形容词存在。

senses.title: Bawdy house
senses.definition: a house of prostitution, in older usage
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对妓院的称呼
senses.example: The old map marks a bawdy house by the docks.
senses.exampleCN: 旧地图在码头边标着一家妓院。
senses.why: The trade's place took the trade's name.
senses.whyCN: 行业场所沿用行业之名。

senses.title: Shakespearean bawdry
senses.definition: the earthy comic strain in Elizabethan drama
senses.definitionCN: 伊丽莎白时代戏剧中的俚俗诙谐
senses.example: The nurse in Romeo and Juliet deals in bawdy wordplay.
senses.exampleCN: 《罗密欧与朱丽叶》里的奶妈满口荤俏皮话。
senses.why: The stage laughed where the church frowned.
senses.whyCN: 舞台在教会皱眉处放声大笑。

senses.title: Bawdy comedy as genre
senses.definition: comedy built on coarse sexual humor
senses.definitionCN: 以粗俗性幽默为骨的喜剧
senses.example: The film is broad bawdy comedy.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影是彻头彻尾的荤喜剧。
senses.why: Genre naming follows the tone word.
senses.whyCN: 类型命名沿用语气之词。

senses.title: Risqué but not obscene
senses.definition: coarse humor that stops short of obscenity
senses.definitionCN: 止于荤而未至淫秽的粗话
senses.example: His after-dinner speech was bawdy, not filthy.
senses.exampleCN: 他餐后致辞有荤，不算下作。
senses.why: Laughter is the valve that keeps bawdy below the law.
senses.whyCN: 笑声是使 bawdy 不越法律之线的阀门。

senses.title: The adverb bawdily
senses.definition: in a coarsely humorous way
senses.definitionCN: 以粗俗诙谐的方式
senses.example: The chronicler tells it bawdily.
senses.exampleCN: 这位记述者把事情讲得颇为荤。
senses.why: The manner suffix carries the tone into narration.
senses.whyCN: 方式后缀把语气带入叙述。

intro.en: Bawdy comes from bawd, a procuress, probably a shortened form of Old French baudet or from Latin fallax, deceitful, via Old French; the adjective records the bawd's earthy trade.
intro.cn: bawdy 出自 bawd「鸨母」，bawd 或为古法语 baudet 的缩略，或经古法语出自拉丁 fallax「欺诈的」；形容词记录了这一行当的俚俗言语。

items.en: fallax meant deceiving; a proposed root.
items.cn: 拉丁 fallax 意为欺诈；一说为词源。

items.en: Old French baude meant bold or merry.
items.cn: 古法语 baude 意为大胆或快活。

items.en: English bawd named the keeper of a brothel.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语 bawd 指妓院主。

items.en: The adjective grew for humor of that trade.
items.cn: 形容词随之而生，指该行当式玩笑。

items.en: Now chiefly a literary classification of coarse humor.
items.cn: 今主要用于指称粗俗幽默的文学类别。

note.en: Group one holds the bawd family and look-alikes; group two holds the coarse-humor field.
note.cn: 第一组收 bawd 词族与形近词；第二组收「粗俗幽默」义场。

entries.definition: the procurer; the root person.
entries.definitionCN: 鸨母；词根本词。

entries.definition: a bald person; from bald.
entries.definitionCN: 秃头者；出 bald，无关。

entries.definition: tastelessly showy; from gaud.

entries.definition: slightly indecent, borderline.
entries.definitionCN: 近乎失度的；略带荤味。

entries.definition: excessively proper about sex.
entries.definitionCN: 过分拘谨的；反义对照。

entries.definition: coarsely amusing about serious matters.
entries.definitionCN: 粗俗打诨的。

normalIntro.cn: bawdy 即 bawd 加 -y：属于老鸨行当的幽默。

normal.en: Degree: bawdier, bawdiest.

abstract.en: The barroom and the stage share one joke.
abstract.cn: 酒馆与舞台同享一个笑话。

examples.en: The film mixes slapstick with bawdy humor.
examples.cn: 影片把打闹与荤段子揉在一起。

examples.en: Chaucer's pilgrims tell bawdy tales.
examples.cn: 乔叟笔下的朝圣者讲着荤故事。

examples.en: Critics praised the play's bawdy energy.
examples.cn: 评论家称赞该剧粗犷泼辣的活力。

definition_zh: 借款人；借入者；借用人；举债方；法律上的借用人
definition_en: a person or organization that takes money or an object from another on the understanding of repayment or return
core_image: 桌子另一端的人接过钱，在纸上写下自己的名字和还款日期
scene: 年轻夫妇在银行签下按揭文件，承诺每月按时偿还。 The borrower missed the first payment and called the bank.
sceneCN: 这里 borrower 指「借款人」（第 1 个义项：取得贷款并承诺偿还的人）；句意为这名借款人错过了第一次还款并致电银行。图中可辨识物件：按揭合同、还款日历、电话、签名笔。

pos.zh: 借款人；借入者；借用人（可数）

senses.title: A person who takes a loan
senses.definition: a person or firm that receives money on a promise to repay it, usually with interest
senses.definitionCN: 接受资金并承诺偿还（通常附利息）的个人或公司
senses.example: The borrower missed the first payment and called the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 这名借款人错过了第一次还款并致电银行。
senses.why: borrow names the receiving side of a loan, and -er marks the one who does it, so the borrower is the taker.
senses.whyCN: borrow 指贷款中的接受方，-er 标记做这件事的人，因此 borrower 是取得一方。

senses.title: One who borrows an object
senses.definition: a person who takes an object for temporary use and is expected to return it
senses.definitionCN: 拿走某物临时使用、并须归还的人
senses.example: The borrower returned the drill the same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 借用人当天晚上就归还了电钻。
senses.why: the word covers any temporary taking, not only money, because borrow never meant money alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词涵盖任何临时取用，不只金钱，因为 borrow 从来不只是指钱。

senses.title: A company or state that issues debt
senses.definition: an entity that raises money by issuing bonds or notes and so becomes the debtor
senses.definitionCN: 通过发行债券或票据筹资、因而成为债务人的实体
senses.example: The borrower sold bonds to refinance old debt.
senses.exampleCN: 这家举债方发行债券以重组旧债。
senses.why: in capital markets the entity that owes the money is called the borrower even when no bank is involved.
senses.whyCN: 在资本市场中，欠款实体即使不经过银行也被称为借款人。

senses.title: A language that takes a word in
senses.definition: in linguistics, the community or language that adopts a word from another language
senses.definitionCN: 语言学上从另一语言吸收词语的社群或语言
senses.example: English is a great borrower of technical terms.
senses.exampleCN: 英语是技术术语的巨大借入者。
senses.why: linguists speak of words as borrowed, so the adopting language becomes the borrower.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把词语说成被借入，于是吸收方语言就成了借入者。

senses.title: One who borrows ideas
senses.definition: a person who takes and uses someone else's idea, method or style
senses.definitionCN: 取用他人想法、方法或风格的人
senses.example: The young painter was a borrower of older styles.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻画家借用较早的风格。
senses.why: ideas travel like objects: they are taken, used and often returned in altered form.
senses.whyCN: 想法像物件一样流动：被取走、使用，常以改变后的形态归还。

senses.title: The party who borrows in law
senses.definition: in bailment for use, the party who receives property for temporary use without gaining ownership
senses.definitionCN: 在使用借贷关系中临时取得财产使用、但不获得所有权的一方
senses.example: The borrower must return the machine in good order.
senses.exampleCN: 借用人必须完好归还这台机器。
senses.why: law needs a precise opposite to the lender, and it uses the everyday word for the receiving side.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个与出借人精确相对的词，于是采用了表示接受方的日常词。

senses.title: A library patron
senses.definition: a person who takes books or media from a library on loan
senses.definitionCN: 从图书馆借走书籍或资料的人
senses.example: Every borrower may renew a book twice.
senses.exampleCN: 每位借阅者可以续借两次。
senses.why: libraries were among the first institutions to use the word for ordinary object loans.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆是最早把这词用于普通物品出借的机构之一。

senses.title: One who relies on others, figuratively
senses.definition: figuratively, a person who depends on resources, courage or meaning supplied by someone else
senses.definitionCN: 比喻上指依赖他人提供的资源、勇气或意义的人
senses.example: Every borrower of courage eventually has to repay it.
senses.exampleCN: 每个借来勇气的人最终都得偿还。
senses.why: the metaphor extends borrowing to qualities that cannot be owned, only drawn on.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把借入扩展到无法拥有、只能取用的品质。

intro.en: Borrower is English borrow plus the agent ending -er. Borrow is native, from Old English borgian, and has no Latin source. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: borrower 是英语 borrow 加施事后缀 -er。borrow 是本族词，来自古英语 borgian，没有拉丁来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Borgian meant 'to borrow' and also 'to lend', because the word first described the pledge given when something was handed over.
items.cn: borgian 既指「借入」也指「借出」，因为这个词最初描述的是交付某物时所给的抵押。

items.en: The related noun borg meant 'pledge, surety'; a loan was secured by a pledge, so the pledge gave the transaction its name.
items.cn: 相关名词 borg 意为「抵押、担保」；贷款以抵押作保，于是抵押给了这笔交易名称。

items.en: The stock appears in Old Norse borga and German borgen, all centred on lending against a pledge.
items.cn: 这套词见于古诺斯语 borga 与德语 borgen，核心都是凭抵押借贷。

items.en: The ending -er is the native agent suffix, and borrower is recorded from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 是本族施事后缀，borrower 自 14 世纪有记录。

items.en: As banking spread, borrower narrowed towards the person who owes money, while the general sense of any borrowed object survived in libraries.
items.cn: 随着银行业普及，borrower 向欠款者收窄，而借任何物品的泛指义在图书馆里留存下来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest record is not precisely dated, and the deeper pre-Germanic origin of borg is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早记录没有确切年代，borg 在日耳曼语之前的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the borrowing stem or words that look close; group two holds the parties and roles that surround a borrower.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「借入」词干或字形相近的形式；第二组是借款人周围的相关方与角色。

entries.definition: To take temporarily; the borrower is the person who does it.
entries.definitionCN: 临时取用；borrower 是做这件事的人。

entries.definition: The act of taking a loan, or the sum taken; it is not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 借入的行为或借入的金额，不是人。

entries.definition: A town with a charter, from Old English burg 'fortified place'; it looks and sounds similar but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 享有特许状的城镇，来自古英语 burg「设防之地」；字形和读音相近，但无关联。

entries.definition: A hole dug by an animal, from Old English byrgian; it resembles borrow only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 动物挖的洞穴，来自古英语 byrgian；仅在拼写上像 borrow。

entries.definition: A person who owes money; a borrower is a debtor while the loan is outstanding, but the words belong to different registers.
entries.definitionCN: 欠款的人；贷款未清时借款人就是债务人，但两个词的使用场合不同。

entries.definition: The party who gives the money or object; the borrower is defined against it.
entries.definitionCN: 给出资金或物品的一方；借款人以之相对定义。

entries.definition: One who holds property under a lease and pays rent; a borrower repays the same thing, a lessee pays for use.
entries.definitionCN: 依租约持有财产并付租金的人；借款人归还原物，承租人则为使用付费。

entries.definition: The borrower who pledges property as security for a mortgage.
entries.definitionCN: 在按揭中以财产作担保的借款人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: borrow + -er: the one who takes temporarily, the mirror of lender.
normal.cn: borrow 加 -er：临时取用的人，与 lender 相对。

normal.en: The family runs borrow, borrowed, borrowing, borrower and borrowings.
normal.cn: 同族包括 borrow、borrowed、borrowing、borrower 与 borrowings。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: a mortgage borrower, a corporate borrower, a borrower defaults.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：按揭借款人、企业借款人、借款人违约。

normal.en: Borrow first meant to give a pledge, so a borrower is someone who has pledged something.
normal.cn: borrow 最初指给出抵押，因此借款人就是曾经押上某物的人。

normal.en: Borrow, borough and burrow look alike but come from different stems.
normal.cn: borrow、borough 与 burrow 形近，却来自不同词干。

abstract.en: Picture a hand taking a coin while a string stays tied to the giver's wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手接过硬币，绳子仍系在给出者的手腕上。

abstract.en: Picture a reader leaving a library with a book that carries a due date.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者带着一本写着到期日的书离开图书馆。

abstract.en: Picture courage as a coat borrowed from a friend and returned at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象勇气是一件向朋友借的外套，在门口归还。

examples.en: The borrower must provide two references.
examples.cn: 借款人必须提供两名推荐人。

examples.en: Corporate borrowers rushed to refinance before rates rose.
examples.cn: 企业借款人在利率上升前争相重组债务。

examples.en: The borrower returned the book two days late.
examples.cn: 借阅者晚了两天才还书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「borrow（借入）+ er（人）」——把东西借进来的人 → 借款人、借用人

root: 古英语 borgian「借入（亦曾指借出）」+ 本族施事后缀 -er；borgian 与名词 borg「抵押、担保」相关，核心是凭抵押借贷。无拉丁来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one role: the person on the receiving side of a temporary transfer, whether money, an object, a bond issue, a word, an idea or a quality.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个角色展开：临时转移中处于接受方的那个人，无论接受的是钱、物件、债券、词语、想法，还是一种品质。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taking a coin while the string stays tied to the giver.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手接过硬币，绳子仍系在给出者手上。

branches.en: THE PERSON WHO TAKES: money and objects are taken on the same promise to give back.
branches.cn: 取用的人：钱与物件都按同一个归还承诺被取走。

branches.en: THE ENTITY THAT OWES: a bond issuer is a borrower even without a bank.
branches.cn: 欠款的实体：债券发行者即使不经过银行也是借款人。

branches.en: WORDS AND IDEAS: a language and a painter both take what others made.
branches.cn: 词语与想法：一种语言与一位画家都取用他人所造之物。

branches.en: LAW AND LIBRARIES: the legal user and the library patron are everyday cases of temporary taking.
branches.cn: 法律与图书馆：合法使用人与图书馆读者都是临时取用的日常情形。

branches.en: BORROWED QUALITIES: courage and meaning can be drawn on but never owned.
branches.cn: 借来的品质：勇气与意义可以取用，却无法拥有。

intro.en: Borrower is a native verb plus a native agent ending; the stem once meant to give a pledge, which is why a borrower is also someone who has pledged.
intro.cn: borrower 是一个本族动词加本族施事词尾；词干原指给出抵押，因此借款人也是曾经押上某物的人。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies behind this family; Latin used mutuum for a loan and creditor or debitor for the parties, all on different roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族背后没有拉丁词；拉丁语用 mutuum 表示贷款，用 creditor 或 debitor 表示双方，词根都不同。
