definition_zh: 文化遗产；世代相传的传统、价值观与实物；受保护的历史建筑与遗址；（法律、政策中的）文化遗产类别
definition_en: the traditions, objects and sites that a society inherits from earlier generations and passes on
core_image: 山谷里的老石屋被一块块补回原样，墙缝里夹着几代人写下的名字
scene: 山谷里的老屋由石匠一块块补回原样，账本上记着每面墙的年代， The trust repairs buildings that belong to the cultural heritage of the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 cultural heritage 指「由先辈留下、需要保护的实物与建筑」（第 2 个义项：物质文化遗产）；句意为该信托机构修缮属于山谷文化遗产的建筑。图中可辨识物件：石墙、脚手架、旧账本、刻字的门楣。

pos.zh: 文化遗产；世代相传的传统与实物；受保护的历史建筑与遗址

forms.label: 复数（多种文化遗产，少见）

senses.title: Traditions and values handed down
senses.titleCN: 世代相传的传统与价值观
senses.definition: the customs, beliefs, stories and values that a community receives from earlier generations
senses.definitionCN: 社群从先辈那里接受的习俗、信念、故事与价值观
senses.example: The songs sung at weddings are part of the cultural heritage of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上唱的歌谣是这座山谷文化遗产的一部分。
senses.why: Heritage begins as a handover: what matters is not the object but the fact that one generation gives it to the next.
senses.whyCN: 遗产起初是一种交接：重要的不是物件本身，而是一代人把它交给下一代这一事实。

senses.title: Physical objects, buildings and sites
senses.definition: the material remains, monuments and historic places that a society inherits
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会继承下来的实物遗存、纪念物与历史场所
senses.example: The trust repairs buildings that belong to the cultural heritage of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构修缮属于山谷文化遗产的建筑。
senses.why: The handover image becomes concrete: a wall, a tool or a street can outlive the hands that made it.
senses.whyCN: 交接的意象变得具体：一面墙、一件工具或一条街，可以比造它的手活得更久。

senses.title: An official or legal category
senses.definition: the status given by law or international convention to objects and places judged worth protecting
senses.definitionCN: 法律或国际公约赋予那些被认为值得保护的物件与场所的地位
senses.example: The old town was listed as cultural heritage, which froze the plans for a new road.
senses.exampleCN: 老城被列为文化遗产，这使新路的规划停了下来。
senses.why: Once a list exists, heritage becomes a legal status: a building is not merely old but protected, with duties attached.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了名录，遗产就成为法律地位：一栋建筑不只是旧，而是受保护，并附带义务。

senses.title: The shared legacy that forms identity
senses.definition: the body of inherited culture through which a group recognizes itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体借以认出自身的继承文化总体
senses.example: The language is the most durable part of their cultural heritage.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是他们文化遗产中最持久的部分。
senses.why: Heritage tells a group what it has in common with its dead, and that continuity is what identity is made of.
senses.whyCN: 遗产告诉一个群体它与逝者共有何物，而认同正是由这种连续性构成的。

senses.title: A field of study and management
senses.definition: the professional work of recording, conserving and interpreting inherited culture
senses.definitionCN: 记录、保护与阐释继承文化的专业工作
senses.example: Cultural heritage management decides which ruins to keep and which to let fall.
senses.exampleCN: 文化遗产管理决定哪些废墟保留、哪些任其倒塌。
senses.why: Heritage needs experts because keeping something costs money and involves choices that pure sentiment cannot make.
senses.whyCN: 遗产需要专家，因为保存要花钱，还要做出单凭感情无法作出的选择。

senses.title: Heritage as tourism and industry
senses.titleCN: 作为旅游与产业的遗产
senses.definition: inherited culture marketed as an attraction for visitors
senses.definitionCN: 被包装成游客吸引物的继承文化
senses.example: Cultural heritage pays for the roof repairs, but it also fills the square with buses.
senses.exampleCN: 文化遗产付得起屋顶修缮费，却也让广场停满大巴。
senses.why: The same handover can be sold: visitors pay to see what earlier generations left, and the money changes the place.
senses.whyCN: 同一种交接也可以出售：游客付费看先辈留下的东西，而钱又改变了这个地方。

senses.title: Family and community memory
senses.definition: the private or local memory, language and stories that a family or small community passes on
senses.definitionCN: 家庭或小社群传递的私人或地方记忆、语言与故事
senses.example: Her grandmother's recipes are cultural heritage at the scale of one kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母的菜谱是只属于一间厨房的文化遗产。
senses.why: Heritage does not require a monument: a recipe, a dialect or a name can be handed down with the same care.
senses.whyCN: 遗产不一定需要纪念碑：一张菜谱、一种方言或一个名字，也可以用同样的心意传下去。

senses.title: Digital heritage
senses.definition: inherited culture recorded, stored or reconstructed in digital form
senses.definitionCN: 以数字形式记录、保存或重建的继承文化
senses.example: The archive's cultural heritage now includes scans of every clay tablet.
senses.exampleCN: 该档案馆的文化遗产如今包括每一块泥板的扫描件。
senses.why: When the record itself becomes the thing kept, heritage moves from stone to server without losing the handover.
senses.whyCN: 当记录本身成为被保存之物，遗产就从石头移到服务器，而交接并没有消失。

intro.en: Cultural heritage joins cultural, from Latin cultura, with heritage, from Latin heres, heir, through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultural heritage 由 cultural 与 heritage 结合而成；cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura，heritage 经法语来自拉丁语 heres「继承人」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Heres meant heir. Its deeper origin is source uncertain; it is not securely connected to any other Latin root.
items.cn: heres 意为「继承人」。它更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠地联系到任何其他拉丁词根。

items.en: Hereditare meant to inherit or to leave by will, built on the noun for heir and its stem hered-.
items.cn: hereditare 意为「继承、按遗嘱留下」，由表示继承人的名词及其词干 hered- 构成。

items.en: Old French eritage named an inherited estate and passed into Middle English as heritage.
items.cn: 古法语 eritage 指继承得来的产业，后进入中古英语，成为 heritage。

items.en: English heritage first meant inherited property and later widened to customs, language and shared past.
items.cn: 英语 heritage 最初指继承的财产，后来扩展到习俗、语言与共有的过去。

items.en: Cultural heritage became a standard term in the twentieth century as states and international bodies began listing what should be protected.
items.cn: 随着国家与国际机构开始编制应受保护的名录，cultural heritage 在二十世纪成为标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of the full phrase is not securely dated, and the origin of heres remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：完整短语在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；heres 的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the heir root; the second holds terms for inherited culture with a different emphasis.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在「继承人」词根上的词；第二组是强调重点不同的继承文化术语。

entries.definition: Inherited property or tradition in general; cultural heritage specifies that the inheritance is cultural rather than financial.
entries.definitionCN: 一般意义上的继承财产或传统；cultural heritage 指明继承的是文化而非财物。

entries.definition: To receive property, traits or traditions from a predecessor; it names the act, while the phrase names what is received.
entries.definitionCN: 从前人那里接受财产、性状或传统；它指动作，而短语指所接受之物。

entries.definition: The property or traits received, especially in law or genetics; it is narrower and more technical than cultural heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 所接受的财产或性状，尤其在法律或遗传学中；它比 cultural heritage 更窄、更技术化。

entries.definition: Transmitted from parent to child, especially of titles or disease; it stresses biological or legal descent, not culture.
entries.definitionCN: 由父母传给子女，尤其指头衔或疾病；它强调生理或法律传承，而非文化。

entries.definition: Something handed down from a predecessor, often with a personal or historical tone; cultural heritage is the collective and public version.
entries.definitionCN: 前人留下之物，常带个人或历史语气；cultural heritage 是集体、公共的版本。

entries.definition: An inheritance from ancestors, often used of national or religious property; more formal and more legal than cultural heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 祖先传下的遗产，常用于国家或宗教财产；比 cultural heritage 更正式、更法律化。

entries.definition: A custom or belief passed down by practice; tradition is one part of cultural heritage, not the whole collection.
entries.definitionCN: 通过实践传下的习俗或信念；传统是文化遗产的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: In law, movable or immovable objects of cultural value; it is the legal counterpart of the broader cultural heritage.
entries.definitionCN: 法律上具有文化价值的可动或不可动物件；它是更宽的 cultural heritage 在法律上的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real heir root, the real family and the phrases the term actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「继承人」词根、真实的同族词，以及这个术语实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: heritage comes from the word for heir: what is handed to the next generation is an inheritance.
normal.cn: heritage 来自表示「继承人」的词：交给下一代的东西就是一份继承。

normal.en: The family runs heritage, inherit, inheritance, hereditary and inheritor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 heritage（遗产）、inherit（继承）、inheritance（继承、遗产）、hereditary（世袭的、遗传的）、inheritor（继承人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: cultural heritage site, intangible cultural heritage, cultural heritage management.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：文化遗产地、非物质文化遗产、文化遗产管理。

normal.en: The phrase covers both songs and stone: not everything inherited is an object.
normal.cn: 这个短语既包括歌谣，也包括石头：并非所有被继承的东西都是物件。

normal.en: Its legal twin is cultural property, which is narrower and protects objects.
normal.cn: 它在法律上的对应词是 cultural property（文化财产），后者更窄，保护的是物件。

abstract.en: Picture a handover across a generation, with one pair of hands letting go as another closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一次跨代的交接：一双手松开，另一双手合拢。

abstract.en: Picture a wall made of stones that each carry a different name.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，每块石头上都刻着不同的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a song written on a clay tablet and also saved on a server.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌既写在泥板上，也保存在服务器里。

examples.en: The language school treats the dialect as living cultural heritage, not a museum piece.
examples.cn: 这所语言学校把方言当作活的文化遗产，而不是博物馆展品。

examples.en: Cultural heritage law can protect a street better than it protects the people who live there.
examples.cn: 文化遗产法保护一条街的能力，可能胜过保护住在那里的人。

examples.en: The digital archive makes cultural heritage available to schools across the province.
examples.cn: 数字档案让全省的学校都能接触文化遗产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「文化的」加「遗产」——先辈传下来的歌谣、老屋与手艺，就是文化遗产。

root: 由 cultural 与 heritage 组成。cultural 来自拉丁语 cultura「耕作、照料」，再往前是 colere「耕种、敬拜」；heritage 经古法语 eritage 来自拉丁语 heres「继承人」，更早的 hered- 词干与 hereditas「继承」相关，而 heres 的来源本身不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one handover: traditions, objects, legal status, identity, management, tourism, family memory and finally the digital record.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次交接展开：传统、实物、法律地位、认同、管理、旅游、家庭记忆，最后是数字记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand letting go of a stone while another hand closes around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开石头，另一只手合拢接住。

branches.en: INTANGIBLE AND PRIVATE: songs, recipes and dialects are handed down in kitchens and villages, not only in museums.
branches.cn: 无形与私人：歌谣、菜谱与方言在厨房和村庄里传下，不只在博物馆里。

branches.en: MATERIAL: walls and tools outlive their makers and become the visible part of the handover.
branches.cn: 物质：墙与工具比制作者活得更久，成为交接中可见的部分。

branches.en: STATUS AND IDENTITY: a listing turns an old place into a protected category, and a shared past into a group's image of itself.
branches.cn: 地位与认同：名录把一处旧地变成受保护的类别，也把共有的过去变成一个群体的自我形象。

branches.en: MANAGEMENT: experts decide what to keep, what to repair and what to let fall.
branches.cn: 管理：专家决定保留什么、修缮什么、任其倒塌什么。

branches.en: SALE AND SCAN: heritage can be sold to visitors or stored as data, but the handover remains.
branches.cn: 出售与扫描：遗产可以卖给游客，也可以存为数据，但交接仍在。

intro.en: Cultural heritage is a culture adjective plus an inheritance noun, and the inheritance noun has its own family.
intro.cn: cultural heritage 是一个文化形容词加一个继承名词，而这个继承名词又有自己的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres, heir, gives the hered- stem behind heritage, inherit and hereditary; cultura gives cultural.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 heres「继承人」给出 heritage、inherit 与 hereditary 背后的 hered- 词干；cultura 给出 cultural。

items.structure: heres, heredis (m./f., third declension, Latin noun)
items.example: The stem hered- runs through heritage and hereditary.
items.exampleCN: hered- 词干贯穿 heritage 与 hereditary。

items.example: The Latin noun named both the act and the property.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词既指继承行为，也指继承的财产。

items.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will
items.example: The verb produced French hériter and English inherit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词产生了法语 hériter 与英语 inherit。

items.example: The house is part of the family heritage.
items.exampleCN: 这所房子是家族遗产的一部分。

items.example: She inherited the workshop from her uncle.
items.exampleCN: 她从叔叔那里继承了这间作坊。
这份遗产包括那座果园。

items.meaning: passed by blood or by legal descent
items.meaningCN: 由血统或法定世系传下的

items.example: The noun gave English culture and cultural.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给出英语 culture 与 cultural。

items.example: The ending builds cultural and natural.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 cultural（文化的）与 natural（自然的）。

latinEntries.meaning: to inherit; to leave by will

definition_zh: v. 使拥挤，堵塞；使充血
definition_en: to block or fill something so that it cannot flow
core_image: 车流挤在一条过窄的路上动弹不得
scene: 节日的车流会让市中心的道路拥堵不堪。 Festival traffic can congest the roads in the city centre.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：congest 指使堵塞；句意是节日车流会让市中心道路拥堵。

pos.zh: 使拥挤；堵塞；使充血

senses.title: Block a passage
senses.definition: to fill a passage so traffic or flow slows
senses.definitionCN: 把通道塞满，使车流或流动变慢
senses.example: Roadworks congest the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 道路施工让市中心拥堵。
senses.why: Latin congerere means to pile up.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 congerere 意为堆起。

senses.title: Fill with blood
senses.definition: to make a part of the body too full of blood
senses.definitionCN: 使身体某处血液过多
senses.example: A cold congested his chest.
senses.exampleCN: 感冒让他的胸口充血。
senses.why: The sense keeps the idea of piling up inside.
senses.whyCN: 该义保留「在内部堆积」之意。

intro.en: Congest comes from Latin congerere, to pile together.
intro.cn: congest 源自拉丁语 congerere，意为堆在一起。

items.en: Gerere means to carry.
items.cn: gerere 意为携带。

items.en: Congerere means to pile up.
items.cn: congerere 意为堆积。

items.en: Congestus is the piled mass.
items.cn: congestus 指堆起的一团。

items.en: English used congest of crowded parts.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用它指拥挤的部位。

items.en: Medicine applied it to blood and lungs.
items.cn: 十九世纪医学用于血液与肺。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the congest stem; the near-meaning group names blocking and loading.
note.cn: 形近组共享 congest 词干；近义组列出堵塞与装载。

entries.definition: The state of being blocked.
entries.definitionCN: 堵塞的状态。

entries.definition: Blocked or overcrowded.
entries.definitionCN: 堵塞或拥挤的。

entries.definition: To swallow food or drink.
entries.definitionCN: 吞下食物或饮料。

entries.definition: To stop movement through.
entries.definitionCN: 阻断通行。

entries.definition: To fill a channel and stop it.
entries.definitionCN: 塞住通道。

entries.definition: To press so movement stops.
entries.definitionCN: 挤住使不能动。

entries.definition: To load beyond capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 装载过多。

normalIntro.en: Congest piles things into a space until nothing moves.
normalIntro.cn: congest 把东西堆进空间，直到一切都动不了。

normal.en: Congerere means to pile up.
normal.cn: congerere 意为堆积。

normal.en: Cars pile up on one road.
normal.cn: 车辆挤上同一条路。

normal.en: Blood can pile up in a lung.
normal.cn: 血也会积在肺里。

normal.en: Congest is the verb; congestion is the state.
normal.cn: congest 是动作，congestion 是状态。

normal.en: The picture is always a full channel.
normal.cn: 其意象总是「塞满的通道」。

abstract.en: A funnel packed with sand.
abstract.cn: 塞满沙子的漏斗。

abstract.en: A doorway filled with shoulders.
abstract.cn: 被肩膀堵住的门洞。

abstract.en: A pipe narrowing under pressure.
abstract.cn: 受压变窄的管道。

examples.en: Weekend traffic congests the bridge.
examples.cn: 周末车流让大桥拥堵。

examples.en: The cold congested his lungs.
examples.cn: 感冒使他的肺部充血。

examples.en: New rules may congest the market.
examples.cn: 新规可能让市场拥堵。

dict_mnemonic.text: con（一起）+ gest（携带、堆积）→ 全都堆到一起，即堵塞。

root: 拉丁 con（一起）+ gerere（携带）→ congerere（堆积）→ 英语 congest

sensesIntro.en: Piling so much into a channel that the flow stops.
sensesIntro.cn: 往通道里堆得太多，流动因此停下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cars packed nose to tail on one road
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆挨一辆挤在同一条路上

branches.en: A road that cannot move.
branches.cn: 动弹不得的道路。

branches.en: A port with ships waiting.
branches.cn: 船只等待的港口。

branches.en: A chest tight with a cold.
branches.cn: 因感冒发紧的胸口。

branches.en: A nose blocked at night.
branches.cn: 夜里堵住的鼻子。

branches.en: Filling past the point of flow.
branches.cn: 超过流动极限的填塞。

intro.en: Congest joins con- to the carrying root gerere.
intro.cn: congest 把 con- 接到表「携带」的 gerere 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin gerere is to carry and congerere is to pile up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gerere 意为携带，congerere 意为堆积。

definition_zh: 学徒；见习生；初学者
definition_en: a person who learns a trade from a skilled employer for a fixed period
core_image: 工坊里的少年：白天递工具、擦长凳，夜里偷偷练手艺
scene: 铁匠铺里炉火通红，老匠人把一把新锉刀放进少年手中。 The blacksmith took on an apprentice to pass on his craft.
sceneCN: 这里 apprentice 是「学徒」（第 1 个义项：跟师傅学手艺的人）；句意为：铁匠收了一名学徒来传承手艺。

pos.zh: 学徒；见习生；生手
使当学徒

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ship，义为「学徒期；学徒身份」
过去分词转形容词，义为「当过学徒的」

senses.title: A learner of a trade
senses.definition: someone bound to work for a master in order to learn a craft
senses.definitionCN: 签约跟随师傅做工以学手艺的人
senses.example: The apprentice swept the shop before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 学徒天亮前就把店铺扫净了。
senses.why: Learning happens by holding, so the learner is taken into the master's hands.
senses.whyCN: 学习靠亲手握持，所以学手艺的人被交到师傅手中。

senses.title: A trainee in a profession
senses.definition: a beginner gaining supervised experience in a modern occupation
senses.definitionCN: 在现代行业里接受指导积累经验的初学者
senses.example: She spent a year as an apprentice electrician.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了一年电工见习生。
senses.why: Old workshop bonds became modern supervised training.
senses.whyCN: 旧式工坊契约演变为现代的带教训练。

senses.title: A beginner without skill
senses.definition: a person with little experience in any activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某种活动中缺乏经验的人
senses.example: In the kitchen I am still an apprentice.
senses.exampleCN: 在厨房里我仍是生手。
senses.why: Anyone still holding the tools awkwardly is like a bound learner.
senses.whyCN: 握工具还笨拙的人，就像尚未出师的学徒。

senses.title: To bind someone as a learner
senses.definition: to arrange for a person to train under a master
senses.definitionCN: 安排某人到师傅门下受训
senses.example: His father apprenticed him to a printer.
senses.exampleCN: 他父亲送他去印刷匠门下当学徒。
senses.why: The holding works both ways: the master takes hold of the learner.
senses.whyCN: 握持是双向的：师傅也把学徒「握」在门下。

senses.title: To learn by serving
senses.definition: to acquire skill while doing humble work for an expert
senses.definitionCN: 在为行家打杂的过程中习得技能
senses.example: He apprenticed in a Paris bakery for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在巴黎一家面包坊学徒两年。
senses.why: Service is the price of the secrets held by the master.
senses.whyCN: 服杂役是换取师傅独门技艺的代价。

senses.title: A member of a guild's junior rank
senses.definition: historically, the lowest rank of a guild, below journeyman and master
senses.definitionCN: 旧时行会中低于熟练工与师傅的最低等级
senses.example: Every guild apprentice hoped to rise to master.
senses.exampleCN: 每个行会学徒都盼着升为师傅。
senses.why: The ladder of holding: first you are held, then you hold the trade.
senses.whyCN: 握持的阶梯：先被师傅握管，再由你握住整门手艺。

senses.title: One under a legal contract
senses.definition: a person bound by a formal indenture specifying duties and years
senses.definitionCN: 受正式契约规定职责与年限约束的人
senses.example: The apprentice signed papers binding him for seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 学徒签署了约束他七年的文书。
senses.why: Legal papers hold both master and learner to the bond.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书把师徒双方都约束在契约之中。

senses.title: An eager follower of a master
senses.definition: figuratively, a devotee learning from someone admired in any field
senses.definitionCN: 比喻在任意领域追随仰慕者学习的人
senses.example: Young poets served as apprentices to the old master's style.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻诗人们模仿老大师的风格学习。
senses.why: Any field with masters can bind learners to them.
senses.whyCN: 凡有大师之处，皆可有门徒相随。

intro.en: Apprentice comes through Old French aprendre, to learn, from Latin apprehendere, to grasp or seize.
intro.cn: apprentice 经古法语 aprendre（学习）而来，词源是拉丁语 apprehendere（抓住、把握）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ghend- meant to seize or take hold.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ghend- 意为抓住、握取。

items.en: Apprehendere, ad- plus prehendere, meant to grasp, both with the hand and with the mind.
items.cn: apprehendere 由 ad- 加 prehendere 构成，既指用手抓取，也指用心把握。

items.en: Apprendere became aprendre, to learn; aprendiz meant one who is learning.
items.cn: apprendere 演变为 aprendre（学习）；aprendiz 指正在学习的人。

items.en: English borrowed apprentice for learners bound to masters of trades.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入 apprentice，指签约从师的学艺人。

items.en: It now covers trade learners, professional trainees, and any humble beginner.
items.cn: 如今涵盖手艺学徒、行业见习生以及任何生手。

note.en: Apprentice descends from the prehend family of grasping words.
note.cn: apprentice 源自 prehend「抓取」词族。

entries.definition: the period or state of being an apprentice
entries.definitionCN: 学徒期；学徒身份

entries.definition: to arrest someone; to grasp mentally
entries.definitionCN: 逮捕；领会

entries.definition: to grasp fully with the mind
entries.definitionCN: 充分理解

entries.definition: a person being trained for a job
entries.definitionCN: 受训者；实习生

entries.definition: a beginner in any activity
entries.definitionCN: 新手；生手

entries.definition: a student working for supervised experience
entries.definitionCN: 实习生

normalIntro.en: Trace apprentice back to grasping, and every sense follows.
normalIntro.cn: 把 apprentice 追溯到「抓取」，一切义项便顺理成章。

normal.en: apprentice = ap- (toward) + prehend (grasp): one taken in to learn.
normal.cn: apprentice = ap-（朝向）+ prehend（抓取）：被收进来学艺的人。

normal.en: Same root as apprehend, comprehend, prehensile.
normal.cn: 与 apprehend、comprehend、prehensile 同根。

normal.en: The verb pattern: apprentice someone to a master.
normal.cn: 动词句式：apprentice someone to a master（送某人拜师）。

normal.en: Suffix pair: apprentice → apprenticeship, like friend → friendship.
normal.cn: 后缀配对：apprentice→apprenticeship，如同 friend→friendship。

normal.en: Guild ladder: apprentice, journeyman, master.
normal.cn: 行会阶梯：学徒、熟练工、师傅。

abstract.en: A small hand gripping a huge hammer — learning starts with holding on.
abstract.cn: 一只小手攥着大锤——学习从握住开始。

abstract.en: A brain with a hand attached: to learn is to grasp twice.
abstract.cn: 长着手的大脑：学习就是两次抓取。

abstract.en: Apprentice sounds like 'a prentice'; just drop the first vowel mentally.
abstract.cn: apprentice 听着像 a prentice，心里去掉首音即可。

examples.en: The apprentice learned the trade in seven hard years.
examples.cn: 学徒在艰苦的七年里学会了这门手艺。

examples.en: She was apprenticed to a master jeweler at fifteen.
examples.cn: 她十五岁就拜在珠宝大师门下当学徒。

examples.en: Even masters once worked as apprentices.
examples.cn: 大师们都曾做过学徒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿伦提斯」——阿伦提着工具箱去拜师当学徒，谐音仅助记。

root: 拉丁词根 prehens-/prehend-（抓取、握住）：apprentice 经古法语 aprendre（学习）源自 apprehendere（用手与心去把握），本义「正在把握手艺的人」，即学徒。

sensesIntro.en: From grasping a craft under a master, apprentice extends to professional trainees, unskilled beginners, binding others to learn, learning through service, guild ranks, legal indenture, and figurative discipleship.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「在师傅手下把握手艺」出发，apprentice 延伸到行业见习生、生手、使拜师、在服务中学习、行会等级、契约约束以及比喻性的门徒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a learner's hand gripping the tools under a master's eye
core.cn: 核心意象：学徒的手在师傅注视下握住工具

branches.en: learning a trade or profession under supervision
branches.cn: 在指导下学手艺或学专业

branches.en: beginners and figurative followers in any field
branches.cn: 任何领域的新手与比喻性门徒

branches.en: the two-way bond: being bound and learning by serving
branches.cn: 双向纽带：被收徒与在服务中学习

branches.en: the bottom rung of the guild ladder
branches.cn: 行会阶梯的最底层

branches.en: the legal paper that holds both sides
branches.cn: 约束双方的契约文书

intro.en: Apprentice carries the prehend root shared by seize-words and mind-words alike.
intro.cn: apprentice 携带 prehend 词根，抓取类词与心智类词共享此根。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere, to seize, is the engine behind apprehend, comprehend, and prehensile.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prehendere（抓住）是 apprehend、comprehend、prehensile 的动力核心。

items.meaning: to seize; to grasp with the mind

items.example: He comprehended the theory at once.
items.exampleCN: 他立刻领悟了这一理论。

definition_zh: 缺乏；不足；缺陷；不足额
definition_en: a lack or shortage of something needed, or a fault that makes something incomplete
core_image: 木桶侧壁缺了一块，水位低于刻度线
scene: 体检报告上有一栏偏低： Iron deficiency is common among children in the region.
sceneCN: 这里 deficiency 是「缺乏」（第 2 个义项：营养素摄入不足）；句意：该地区儿童缺铁很常见。图中可辨识物件：木桶缺口、低于刻度的水位、血检报告、铁剂药瓶、儿童身高尺。

pos.zh: 缺乏；不足；缺陷；（账目）不足额

senses.title: A lack of something needed
senses.definition: the state of not having enough of something that is necessary
senses.definitionCN: 必需之物数量不足的状态
senses.example: The report identifies a deficiency of trained staff.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出受训人员不足。
senses.why: Latin deficere means 'to fail or be lacking', from de- 'away' and facere 'to do'. Something is missing, so the job cannot be done, and the noun names that gap.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 deficere 意为“失败、缺少”，由 de-“离开”与 facere“做”构成。某物缺失，事情就做不成，名词命名的正是这个缺口。

senses.title: A nutrient deficiency
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏：身体缺某种养分
senses.definition: a shortage of a nutrient required for health
senses.definitionCN: 健康所需的某种营养素不足
senses.example: Iron deficiency is common among children in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区儿童缺铁很常见。
senses.why: The body is a system that needs inputs; when one input falls below the needed level, the gap is named by the nutrient that is missing.
senses.whyCN: 身体是需要输入的系统；当某项输入低于所需水平，缺口就用缺失的那种营养素来命名。

senses.title: Immune deficiency
senses.titleCN: 免疫缺陷：防线缺了一块
senses.definition: a weakness or absence in the body's immune defences
senses.definitionCN: 身体免疫防线的薄弱或缺失
senses.example: The treatment is designed for patients with immune deficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 该疗法专为免疫缺陷患者设计。
senses.why: The 'gap in the wall' image becomes medical: a missing part of the defence lets infection in, so the deficiency is a structural hole rather than a low number.
senses.whyCN: “墙上的缺口”意象进入医学：防线缺一部分，感染便能进入，因此缺陷是结构性的洞，而不只是数值偏低。

senses.title: A defect in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：设计或系统里的毛病
senses.definition: a fault or weakness that makes something incomplete or ineffective
senses.definitionCN: 使某物不完整或失效的缺点或薄弱处
senses.example: The audit found a deficiency in the control system.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现控制系统中存在缺陷。
senses.why: Deficiency can point to a missing part rather than a missing quantity: the thing is not merely low on stock, it lacks a piece it needs to work.
senses.whyCN: deficiency 也可指缺了一个部件，而非数量不足：该物不只是存量少，而是缺少工作所需的零件。

senses.title: A deficiency judgment
senses.titleCN: 不足额判决：拍卖款不够还债
senses.definition: in law, a judgment ordering a debtor to pay the balance left after property is sold
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指财产变卖后仍欠余额、判令债务人补足的判决
senses.example: The bank obtained a deficiency judgment for the remaining balance.
senses.exampleCN: 银行就剩余余额获得了不足额判决。
senses.why: Foreclosure recovers part of a debt; the rest is still missing. The legal phrase names the gap that the court orders the debtor to close.
senses.whyCN: 止赎只能收回部分债务，其余仍然缺失。这个法律短语命名的正是法院命令债务人补上的缺口。

senses.title: A revenue shortfall
senses.definition: an amount by which income falls short of what is needed or expected
senses.definitionCN: 收入低于所需或预期数额的差额
senses.example: The city faces a budget deficiency of ten million dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 该市面临一千万美元的预算缺口。
senses.why: Accounts compare what should be there with what is there. The difference is a hole in the total, and deficiency names it more formally than shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 账目把应有的数额与实际数额相比。差额就是总数上的洞，deficiency 比 shortfall 更正式地命名它。

senses.title: An audit finding
senses.titleCN: 审计缺陷：内控上的可报告问题
senses.definition: in auditing, a weakness in internal controls serious enough to be reported
senses.definitionCN: 审计中严重到需要报告内部控制薄弱之处
senses.example: The auditors listed two material deficiencies in reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师列出了报告方面的两项重大缺陷。
senses.why: Audit language treats a missing control as a gap through which error can pass. The word is technical because the gap is defined by a standard, not by a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 审计语言把缺失的控制视为让错误穿过的缺口。这个词之所以技术化，是因为缺口由标准界定，而非凭感觉。

senses.title: A deficiency disease
senses.titleCN: 营养缺乏病：缺某物直接致病
senses.definition: a disease caused by the absence of a specific nutrient
senses.definitionCN: 因缺少特定营养素而直接引起的疾病
senses.example: Scurvy is a classic deficiency disease caused by lack of vitamin C.
senses.exampleCN: 坏血病是缺乏维生素 C 引起的典型营养缺乏病。
senses.why: The compound joins the gap to its consequence: remove one necessary input and the body fails in a recognizable pattern, which medicine names after the missing item.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把缺口与后果连起来：去掉一项必需输入，身体就以可识别的方式衰竭，医学便以缺失物来命名疾病。

intro.en: Deficiency is deficient + -cy, from Latin deficientia, built on deficere 'to fail, be lacking'. The same verb gives deficit and defect.
intro.cn: deficiency 是 deficient + -cy，来自拉丁 deficientia，建立在 deficere“失败、缺少”上。同一动词还产生 deficit 与 defect。

items.en: deficere 'to fail, run short, desert' combines de- 'away' and facere 'to do, make'. The picture is something withdrawing from where it is needed, so the task is left undone.
items.cn: deficere“失败、短缺、背离”由 de-“离开”与 facere“做、造”组成。画面是某物从需要它的地方撤走，任务便无法完成。

items.en: deficientia 'a failing, a lack' is the abstract noun. English forms deficiency with the French-Latin ending -cy, as in other -cy nouns.
items.cn: deficientia“失败、缺乏”是抽象名词。英语用法语—拉丁来源的 -cy 词尾构成 deficiency，与其他 -cy 名词一致。

items.en: English deficiency is recorded from the 17th century in medical and administrative writing. The exact first date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 deficiency 在17世纪的医学与行政文本中已有记录。最早确切年代为约数。

items.en: The 19th and 20th centuries fixed deficiency disease and nutrient deficiency as medicine learned to identify specific missing substances.
items.cn: 19、20世纪，随着医学学会识别具体缺失物质，deficiency disease 与 nutrient deficiency 固定下来。

items.en: Deficiency judgment and budget deficiency extend the word to money: the amount by which a fund or payment falls short of what is owed.
items.cn: deficiency judgment 与 budget deficiency 把这个词延伸到金钱：资金或付款低于应付数额的差额。

items.en: The exact semantic path from 'failing' to 'structural defect' is not fully documented. The deeper PIE origin of facere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 从“失败”到“结构缺陷”的确切语义路径没有完整记录。facere 的更早印欧语来源属重构。

note.en: The first group contains the same-root nouns that are often confused in finance and law; the second contains shortage words with different scopes.
note.cn: 第一组是同根名词，在金融与法律语境中常被混淆；第二组是范围不同的“短缺”类词。

entries.definition: The amount by which spending exceeds income; it is usually a financial figure, while deficiency can also be a defect or a nutrient lack.
entries.definitionCN: 支出超过收入的差额；通常是财务数字，而 deficiency 也可指缺陷或营养缺乏。

entries.definition: A fault that makes a product or plan imperfect; it is countable and concrete, closer to sense 4.
entries.definitionCN: 使产品或计划不完美的毛病；可数且具体，更接近第 4 个义项。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'lacking'; deficiency is the noun for the lack itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“缺乏的”的形容词；deficiency 是“缺乏”本身的名词。

entries.definition: A situation in which supply is below demand; it is usually temporary and economic.
entries.definitionCN: 供应低于需求的情形；通常为暂时的经济现象。

entries.definition: The absence of something; the most general word, without the technical or medical frame.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不存在；最通用的词，没有技术或医学框架。

entries.definition: The amount by which a target is missed; it names a figure, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 未达到目标的差额；命名的是一个数字，而非状态。

entries.definition: The quality of being insufficient for a purpose; it often carries a judgment of quality.
entries.definitionCN: 对某用途而言不够的性质；常带质量判断。

entries.definition: A point that can be attacked or can fail; it is broader than a technical deficiency.
entries.definitionCN: 可被攻击或可能失效的点；比技术意义上的 deficiency 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, standard collocations and the deficere family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、标准搭配与 deficere 词族。

normal.en: de- 'away' + facere 'do': something has gone away, so the work cannot be done — that is the lack.
normal.cn: de-“离开”+ facere“做”：某物离开了，事情就做不成——这就是缺乏。

normal.en: deficiency, deficit and defect are siblings: a lack, its amount, and the fault it leaves behind.
normal.cn: deficiency、deficit、defect 是同胞词：缺乏、差额、以及留下的毛病。

normal.en: Learn nutrient deficiency, immune deficiency and deficiency disease; these are the medical core.
normal.cn: 记住 nutrient deficiency、immune deficiency、deficiency disease；这些是医学核心搭配。

normal.en: In finance use deficit for the shortfall; in medicine use deficiency for the missing substance.
normal.cn: 财务缺口用 deficit；医学缺失用 deficiency。

normal.en: deficient is the adjective, deficiency the noun, deficiently the adverb.
normal.cn: deficient 是形容词，deficiency 是名词，deficiently 是副词。

abstract.en: Picture a barrel with one plank missing, so the water line can never reach the mark.
abstract.cn: 想象木桶少了一块板，水位线永远到不了刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with one brick pulled out, leaving a gap wide enough for a hand.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上被抽走一块砖，留下一个能伸进手的缺口。

abstract.en: Picture an invoice where the paid amount stops short of the total, leaving a visible balance line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张发票，已付金额没到总额，留下一行清晰的余额。

examples.en: Vitamin D deficiency can weaken the bones over time.
examples.cn: 维生素 D 缺乏会随着时间使骨骼变弱。

examples.en: The review found serious deficiencies in the safety procedures.
examples.cn: 审查发现安全程序存在严重缺陷。

examples.en: The fund was set up to cover a deficiency in local services.
examples.cn: 该基金旨在弥补地方服务的不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: “de（低）+ fic（做）+ iency”——该做的没做到位，桶就缺一块 → deficiency 缺乏、缺陷

root: 拉丁 deficere“失败、缺少”（de-“离开”+ facere“做”）；deficient + -cy 名词后缀，同根词有 deficit、defect。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gap: something needed is not there. The gap may be a nutrient, a defence, a control, a payment or a whole missing part.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个缺口：需要的东西不在。缺口可以是营养、防线、控制、付款，或整个缺失的部件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a missing plank in a barrel, with the water line below the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桶少了一块板，水位低于刻度。

branches.en: DEFECT: a missing part is the same gap measured in structure.
branches.cn: 缺陷：缺失的部件，是缺口在结构层面的度量。

branches.en: BODY: a nutrient below the needed level and an immune defence with a hole both let the system fail.
branches.cn: 身体：营养素低于所需水平、免疫防线有洞，都会让系统失效。

branches.en: MONEY: a deficiency judgment and a budget gap both name the balance that is still missing.
branches.cn: 金钱：不足额判决与预算缺口，都命名仍然缺失的余额。

branches.en: TECHNICAL CONSEQUENCES: an audit deficiency is a missing control; a deficiency disease is the body's failure from a missing nutrient.
branches.cn: 技术后果：审计缺陷是缺失的控制；营养缺乏病是身体因缺营养素而衰竭。

branches.en: GENERAL CORE: the plain sense covers every specialised branch, since each branch is a particular kind of 'not enough'.
branches.cn: 一般核心：平实义覆盖所有专业分支，因为每个分支都是“不够”的某种具体形态。

intro.en: Deficiency is deficient + -cy. The suffix forms abstract nouns of state; the base is the Latin verb deficere, whose de- and fac- are fossilized.
intro.cn: deficiency 是 deficient + -cy。后缀构成状态抽象名词；词基是拉丁动词 deficere，其 de- 与 fac- 已凝固。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do, make' underlies a huge family: efficient, sufficient, deficient, defect, factory, fiction and fashion. The prefix changes whether the doing succeeds or falls short.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere“做、造”支撑着一个庞大词族：efficient、sufficient、deficient、defect、factory、fiction、fashion。前缀决定“做”是成功还是不足。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏；缺陷（-cy 状态名词）
items.example: The deficiency was corrected by adding a supplement.
items.exampleCN: 通过补充剂纠正了这一缺乏。

items.meaningCN: 缺乏的；不足的（-ent 形容词后缀）
items.example: The diet was deficient in calcium.

items.meaning: the amount by which something falls short
items.meaningCN: 赤字；不足额（-it 分词词尾）
items.example: The budget deficit grew for a third year.
items.exampleCN: 预算赤字连续第三年扩大。

items.meaningCN: 缺陷；瑕疵（de-“离开”+ fect-“被造”）
items.example: The defect appeared after two weeks of use.
items.exampleCN: 使用两周后出现了缺陷。

items.meaningCN: 不足地；有缺陷地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: The system performed deficiently under load.
items.exampleCN: 系统在负载下表现不足。

items.example: The new engine is more efficient.
The evidence was sufficient for a verdict.

items.meaning: a place where goods are made
items.example: The factory produces parts for turbines.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产涡轮零件。

items.example: The novel mixes fiction with recorded history.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说把虚构与有记载的历史混合在一起。

definition_zh: 一个文化的神话总体；神话学；也指被广泛相信却不实的观念体系
definition_en: the body of myths belonging to a culture, the study of such myths, and a widely held but unfounded set of beliefs
core_image: 神庙的壁画上画着一位持雷的神，旁边的铭文讲他如何生出大地
scene: 神庙的壁画上画着一位持雷的神，旁边的铭文讲他如何生出大地。 Greek mythology gives the storm god a spear and a short temper.
sceneCN: 这里 mythology 指「一个文化的神话总体」（第 1 个义项：关于神祇与起源的故事集合）；句意为希腊神话赋予这位风暴之神一柄长矛和急躁的脾气。可辨识物件：壁画、雷、长矛、铭文、神庙。

pos.zh: 神话（总体）；神话学
被广泛相信的不实观念体系

senses.title: A culture's body of myths
senses.definition: the whole collection of stories a society tells about gods, heroes and origins
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会关于神祇、英雄与起源的全部故事集合
senses.example: Greek mythology gives the storm god a spear and a short temper.
senses.exampleCN: 希腊神话赋予风暴之神一柄长矛和急躁的脾气。
senses.why: mythos meant a told story and -logia meant an account, so the word first names a body of stories told together.
senses.whyCN: mythos 指被讲述的故事，-logia 指叙述，因此这个词先指被一起讲述的故事总体。

senses.title: The myths of one particular people
senses.definition: the specific myth system of a named culture, such as Greek, Norse or Egyptian
senses.definitionCN: 某个具名文化的特定神话体系，如希腊、北欧或埃及
senses.example: Norse mythology ends with a fire that consumes the world.
senses.exampleCN: 北欧神话以一场吞噬世界的大火结束。
senses.why: each people organizes its stories into a recognisable system with its own gods.
senses.whyCN: 每个民族把自己的故事组织成可辨认的体系，各有其神。

senses.title: The scholarly study of myth
senses.definition: the academic analysis of myths and their meanings, functions and structures
senses.definitionCN: 对神话及其意义、功能与结构进行的学术分析
senses.example: Comparative mythology looks for shared patterns across continents.
senses.exampleCN: 比较神话学在各大洲寻找共同模式。
senses.why: the same -logia that names a field in other disciplines here names the study of myth.
senses.whyCN: -logia 在其他学科中标记领域，这里标记对神话的研究。

senses.title: A widely believed set of ideas
senses.titleCN: 被广泛相信的观念体系
senses.definition: a system of beliefs that a group treats as obvious though it is not proven
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体视为理所当然、却未经证明的信念体系
senses.example: The mythology of endless growth shaped the whole plan.
senses.exampleCN: 无限增长的信念体系塑造了整个计划。
senses.why: modern writers borrowed the word for secular faiths that work like myths.
senses.whyCN: 现代作者借用这个词来指像神话般运作的世俗信仰。

senses.title: A false story people repeat
senses.titleCN: 被反复传播的不实说法（贬义）
senses.definition: used dismissively of an unfounded claim that circulates as if it were fact
senses.definitionCN: 轻蔑地指一种被当作事实传播的无据说法
senses.example: The story that he invented the machine is pure mythology.
senses.exampleCN: 说他发明了那台机器的说法纯属神话。
senses.why: once a story is doubted, mythology becomes a word for comfortable untruth.
senses.whyCN: 一旦故事受到怀疑，mythology 就变成「令人安心的假话」之词。

senses.title: The gods and heroes in a myth system
senses.titleCN: 神话体系中的神祇与英雄
senses.definition: the characters that populate a myth system and carry its values
senses.definitionCN: 填充神话体系并承载其价值观的角色
senses.example: The mythology of the city is crowded with rival patron gods.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的神话挤满了相互竞争的守护神。
senses.why: a system needs actors, and gods and heroes are the actors of myth.
senses.whyCN: 体系需要行动者，而神祇与英雄正是神话的行动者。

senses.title: A creation story
senses.definition: the narrative that explains how the world, life or a people began
senses.definitionCN: 解释世界、生命或一个民族如何开始的叙事
senses.example: Their mythology begins with a bird that drops a grain of sand.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的创世神话始于一只鸟丢下一粒沙。
senses.why: origins are the question myths exist to answer, so creation is their central episode.
senses.whyCN: 起源是神话存在所要回答的问题，因此创世是其核心情节。

senses.title: Recurring motifs and archetypes
senses.definition: the repeated images and patterns that move between myth systems
senses.definitionCN: 在不同神话体系之间流动的重复意象与模式
senses.example: The dying-and-rising god is a common mythology motif.
senses.exampleCN: 死而复生的神是常见的神话母题。
senses.why: comparison needs units smaller than a whole system, and motifs supply them.
senses.whyCN: 比较研究需要小于整个体系的单位，母题正好提供。

senses.title: Myths retold in art and literature
senses.titleCN: 神话在文学艺术中的再创作
senses.definition: the reuse of mythic material by later writers, painters and composers
senses.definitionCN: 后世作家、画家与作曲家对神话材料的再利用
senses.example: Modern opera keeps the old mythology but changes the ending.
senses.exampleCN: 现代歌剧保留古老神话，却改写了结局。
senses.why: myths survive by being retold, so each retelling adds a new layer to the word.
senses.whyCN: 神话靠被重讲而存活，每次重讲都为这个词添上新一层。

intro.en: Mythology comes from Greek mythologia 'a telling of legends', from mythos 'word, story' plus -logia 'an account, a study', through Late Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: mythology 经晚期拉丁语与法语来自希腊 mythologia「讲述传说」，由 mythos「话语、故事」加 -logia「叙述、研究」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mythos meant 'word, speech, tale', without the modern implication of falsehood; the contrast with logos as 'reasoned account' came later.
items.cn: mythos 意为「话语、言说、故事」，起初不含现代「虚假」之意；它与表示「理性叙述」的 logos 的对立是后来才形成的。

items.en: The suffix -logia came from logos 'word, reason' and named an account or study of a subject.
items.cn: 后缀 -logia 出自 logos「言词、理性」，指对某一主题的叙述或研究。

items.en: Mythologia named the telling of legends and the body of such tales, not yet a science of them.
items.cn: mythologia 指传说的讲述与这类故事的整体，尚未指研究它们的科学。

items.en: Late Latin mythologia and French mythologie carried the word into English, where it named both a collection of myths and their study.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 mythologia 与法语 mythologie 把词带入英语，同时指神话集合与对它的研究。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was extended to secular belief systems and finally to any unfounded story.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个词被扩展到世俗信念体系，最终指任何无据的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the earliest use of the dismissive sense is dated only approximately, and the details of the Greek formation are reconstructed from surviving texts.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：贬义的最早用法只有约略年代；希腊语构词细节是根据传世文本重构出来的。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the Greek mythos stem; group two holds narrative and belief terms often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊 mythos 词干的词；第二组是常与之混淆的叙事与信念词。

entries.definition: A single sacred or traditional narrative; mythology is the whole body or the study of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指单则神圣或传统叙事；mythology 指整体或对它的研究。

entries.definition: Means 'of myth' or 'like myth', often used of larger-than-life figures.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「神话的」或「神话般的」，常用于超凡人物。

entries.definition: Relating to mythology as a system or field rather than to one story.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为体系或学科的神话学有关，而非单则故事。

entries.definition: To turn a person or event into myth, or to interpret something mythically.
entries.definitionCN: 指把人或事件神话化，或以神话方式解释某物。

entries.definition: A story about a person or place, told as if it happened; it need not involve gods.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于某人或某地、仿佛真有其事的故事；不必涉及神祇。

entries.definition: Inherited knowledge of any kind; mythology is a particular sacred or origin-focused part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何传承知识；mythology 是其中专注神圣或起源的特定部分。

entries.definition: All the gods of a people taken together, or a temple for them; it is a part of mythology, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个民族全部神祇的集合，或供奉他们的神庙；它是神话的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: The whole inherited culture of ordinary people; mythology is its most sacred and origin-focused strand.
entries.definitionCN: 指普通民众继承的整体文化；mythology 是其中最具神圣性与起源关切的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: mythos 'story' plus -logia 'account' gives 'an account of stories'.
normal.cn: mythos「故事」加 -logia「叙述」，得「对故事的叙述」。

normal.en: The family runs myth, mythic, mythical, mythological, mythologist and mythologize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 myth、mythic、mythical、mythological、mythologist 与 mythologize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: Greek mythology, ancient mythology, comparative mythology, popular mythology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：希腊神话、古代神话、比较神话学、大众流行的错误观念。

normal.en: mythos did not originally mean 'false'; the modern dismissal came much later.
normal.cn: mythos 起初并不表示「虚假」；现代的贬义是后来才有的。

normal.en: A mythology is a system; a myth is one story inside it.
normal.cn: mythology 是一个体系；myth 是体系中的一则故事。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of painted gods, each one explaining a part of the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一面画满神祇的墙，每一位都在解释一部分天气。

abstract.en: Picture a story that a whole city agrees to remember.
abstract.cn: 想象一个整座城市都同意记住的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a comforting belief that nobody has bothered to test.
abstract.cn: 想象一个无人费心去检验的安慰性信念。

examples.en: The course compares creation stories in three mythologies.
examples.cn: 这门课程比较三种神话中的创世故事。

examples.en: The mythology of the frontier still shapes political speech.
examples.cn: 边疆神话至今仍塑造政治话语。

examples.en: His biography separates the man from the mythology around him.
examples.cn: 他的传记把本人与围绕他的神话区分开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「myth（神话）+ ology（学问）」——讲神的故事，也研究这些故事

root: 希腊 mythos「话语、故事」+ -logia「叙述、研究」（出自 logos「言词、理性」）→ 希腊 mythologia → 晚期拉丁 mythologia → 法语 mythologie → 英语 mythology。mythos 原不含「虚假」义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one telling: a people gathers its stories about gods and origins, and that gathering is then read as a system, a science, a secular faith, a false tale, a cast of gods, a creation scene, a motif and a source for art.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一次讲述展开：一个民族把关于神祇与起源的故事聚拢，这个聚拢再依次被读作体系、学科、世俗信仰、假话、神祇群、创世场景、母题与艺术素材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a temple wall where every painted god explains one part of the weather.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面神庙墙壁，每位画中的神都解释一部分天气。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AND ONE PEOPLE'S VERSION: a collection of stories, and the specific system a culture owns.
branches.cn: 整体与某一民族的版本：故事集合，以及一个文化所拥有的特定体系。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the same word names the disciplined look at myth.
branches.cn: 研究：同一个词也指对神话的系统考察。

branches.en: ACTORS AND ORIGINS: gods fill the system, and creation explains why there is a world at all.
branches.cn: 角色与起源：神祇填充体系，创世解释世界为何存在。

branches.en: UNITS AND REUSE: motifs travel between systems, and artists retell them with new endings.
branches.cn: 单位与再利用：母题在体系间流动，艺术家以新结局重讲它们。

branches.en: SECULAR FAITH AND FALSE STORY: when the gods leave, the word can still name a belief people refuse to test.
branches.cn: 世俗信仰与假故事：当神祇离场，这个词仍可指人们拒绝检验的信念。

intro.en: Mythology is two Greek elements joined, one naming a story and one naming an account, and both build large English families.
intro.cn: mythology 由两个希腊成分组合而成，一个指故事，一个指叙述，两者都构成庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek mythos and -logia reached English through Late Latin mythologia and French mythologie, so the Latin forms are borrowings from Greek rather than native Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 mythos 与 -logia 经晚期拉丁 mythologia 与法语 mythologie 进入英语，因此这些拉丁形式是从希腊语借入的，而非拉丁本族词。

items.example: Mythos named a story before it implied a false one.
items.exampleCN: mythos 先指故事，后来才含虚假之意。

items.example: The suffix names fields from biology to theology.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名从生物学到神学的众多领域。

items.example: Logos is the root behind the suffix.
items.exampleCN: logos 是该后缀背后的词根。

items.example: The Greek noun already covered both telling and collecting.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词已同时涵盖讲述与汇集。

items.structure: mythologia, through Late Latin and French
items.meaning: a body of myths; their study
items.example: English merged the two senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 英语把两个义项并入一个词。

items.example: Myth is the countable unit inside mythology.
items.exampleCN: myth 是 mythology 内部的可数单位。

items.example: Mythic means relating to or like myth.
items.exampleCN: mythic 意为与神话有关或像神话的。

items.example: Mythological points at the system or the study.
Mythologize means to turn into myth.

latinEntries.structure: mythologia, mythologiae (f., first declension; Latin borrowing from Greek)
mythicus, mythica, mythicum (adjective, Late Latin from Greek mythikos)
mythos (m., second declension; Latin borrowing from Greek)

definition_zh: n. 血块；凝块；v. 凝结，结块
definition_en: a thick lump formed when blood or another liquid thickens; to form such lumps
core_image: 一滴血在伤口表面慢慢凝成暗红的块
scene: 医生发现他腿上有一处血块。 The doctor found a clot in his leg.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：clot 指血块；句意是医生发现他腿上有一处血块。

pos.zh: 血块；凝块
凝结

senses.title: A thick lump in a liquid
senses.definition: a soft thick mass formed when a liquid thickens
senses.definitionCN: 液体变稠时形成的软而厚的块
senses.example: A blood clot blocked the vein.
senses.exampleCN: 一块血块堵住了血管。
senses.why: Old English clot names a lump or mass.

senses.title: To form lumps

senses.definitionCN: 由液体变成软厚的块状物
senses.example: The sauce clotted when it cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 酱汁冷却后结成了块。
senses.why: The noun of a lump became a verb of lumping.
senses.whyCN: 表示块的名称变成了结成块的动词。

intro.cn: clot 是表示「块」的古老词，后来进入医学与烹饪。

abstract.en: A dark knot inside a river.

definition_zh: n. 山羊绒，开司米；羊绒织物
definition_en: fine soft wool from the Kashmir goat; cloth made from this wool
core_image: 极细的浅色绒毛在指间柔软发亮
scene: 她围上一条浅灰色的羊绒围巾，柔软得像一层雾。 She wrapped a pale grey cashmere scarf around her neck.

definition_zh: 替换；代替；代换；（数学）代入；（化学）取代；（体育）换人
definition_en: the act of putting one person or thing in the place of another
core_image: 棋盘上一枚棋子被另一枚同色棋子换下，方格上的位置标记保持不变
scene: 这里指「替换」。 The coach made a substitution at halftime to strengthen the midfield.
sceneCN: 这里 substitution 是「体育换人」（第 4 个义项：比赛中用替补球员换下场上球员）；句意：教练在半场换人，以加强中场。图中可辨识物件：边线旁的换人牌、第四官员、被换下的球员、替补球员，以及保持不动的中场站位标记。

pos.zh: 替换；代替；代换；（数学）代入；（化学）取代；（体育）换人（指行为时可数，指过程或概念时多不可数）

senses.title: Putting one thing in another's place
senses.titleCN: 替换行为：以他物占据其位
senses.definition: the act of using one person or thing in place of another
senses.definitionCN: 用一个人或物代替另一个的行为
senses.example: The substitution of fresh herbs for dried ones changed the dish.
senses.exampleCN: 用新鲜香草代替干香草改变了这道菜。
senses.why: Latin substituere meant 'to set one thing under or in place of another'; the noun names that placing, not the thing placed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 substituere 意为「把一物置于另一物之下或其位」，名词命名这一放置动作，而不是被放置之物。

senses.title: Substitution into an equation
senses.titleCN: 数学代入：把值放进变量的位置
senses.definition: in algebra, the replacement of a variable by a number or expression
senses.definitionCN: 在代数中用数值或表达式替换变量
senses.example: Substitution of x = 3 gives the value of the expression.
senses.exampleCN: 代入 x = 3 即可得到该表达式的值。
senses.why: Mathematics adopted the word for the mechanical act of putting a value where a symbol stood, which is the literal Latin image of placing one thing in another's position.
senses.whyCN: 数学采用该词表示把数值放到符号原先所在位置的机械动作，这正是拉丁语「置一物于其位」的字面意象。

senses.title: A chemical substitution reaction
senses.titleCN: 化学取代：基团被另一基团换下
senses.definition: a reaction in which one atom or group in a molecule is replaced by another
senses.definitionCN: 分子中一个原子或基团被另一个所替换的反应
senses.example: Nucleophilic substitution replaces the bromide with a hydroxyl group.
senses.exampleCN: 亲核取代用羟基替换溴离子。
senses.why: Chemists keep the word because a group literally leaves and another takes its site on the carbon skeleton, so the Latin idea of placing in position fits the mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 化学家沿用该词，是因为一个基团确实离开，另一个占据它在碳骨架上的位置，拉丁语「置于其位」的思路正好契合这一机理。

senses.title: A player sent on for another
senses.titleCN: 体育换人：替补球员换下场上球员
senses.definition: in team sports, the replacement of one player by another during a match
senses.definitionCN: 团队运动中在比赛进行时用一名球员换下另一名
senses.example: The coach made a substitution at halftime to strengthen the midfield.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在半场换人，以加强中场。
senses.why: Sport borrows the general act and makes it a counted event: a team has a limited number of substitutions, so the noun names both the act and the slot used.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了这一一般动作，并把它变成可计数的赛事事件：球队的换人次数有限，因此名词既指动作，也指用掉的那个名额。

senses.title: The substitution effect in economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学替代效应：转向更便宜的替代品
senses.definition: the change in demand caused by a consumer switching to a cheaper alternative when a price rises
senses.definitionCN: 价格上涨时消费者转向更便宜替代品所引起的需求变化
senses.example: The substitution effect explains why sales of the cheaper brand rose.
senses.exampleCN: 替代效应解释了为什么较便宜品牌的销量上升。
senses.why: Economics turns the act into a named force: one good takes the place of another in the buyer's basket, and the effect is measured separately from income.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把这一动作变成有名称的力量：一种商品在买家的篮子里取代另一种，这一效应与收入效应分开计量。

senses.title: Substitution in language teaching
senses.titleCN: 语言学替换：同一位置上换形式
senses.definition: in linguistics and language teaching, the replacement of one form by another in the same slot, as in a substitution drill
senses.definitionCN: 语言学与语言教学中，用另一形式替换同一位置上的形式，如替换练习
senses.example: The substitution drill swaps one noun for another in the same frame.
senses.exampleCN: 替换练习在同一句型框架内用一个名词换掉另一个。
senses.why: A substitution class is a set of forms that can occupy the same position; the term names the test that identifies the slot.
senses.whyCN: 替换类指能占据同一位置的一组形式；这个术语命名识别该位置的测试。

senses.title: A substitution cipher
senses.titleCN: 密码替换：按规则逐符号替换
senses.definition: a cipher in which each symbol or letter is replaced by another according to a fixed rule
senses.definitionCN: 按固定规则把每个符号或字母替换成另一个的密码
senses.example: A simple substitution cipher is easy to break by counting letter frequencies.
senses.exampleCN: 简单的替换密码很容易通过统计字母频率破解。
senses.why: The cipher is named for the operation, not the key: every unit is systematically replaced, which is the plain sense of substitutio applied to symbols.
senses.whyCN: 这种密码因操作而得名，而非因密钥：每个单元被系统性地替换，这正是 substitutio 用于符号时的字面义。

senses.title: Replacing a party to a contract
senses.titleCN: 合同主体替换：换人而不换义务
senses.definition: in law, the replacement of one party, debtor or obligation by another, often with the consent of the remaining party
senses.definitionCN: 法律中用另一方替换合同一方、债务人或者义务，通常需剩余一方同意
senses.example: The lender agreed to the substitution of a new guarantor.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款方同意更换新的担保人。
senses.why: Contract law needs a precise word for a change of person rather than of terms; substitution marks that the obligation continues while the party occupying it changes.
senses.whyCN: 合同法需要一个精确的词来表示「换人而非换条款」；substitution 标记义务延续、占据该义务的主体发生变更。

intro.en: Substitution comes from Latin substitutio, the action noun of substituere 'to set in place of another', from sub- 'under, instead of' plus statuere 'to set, make stand', which itself comes from stare 'to stand'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: substitution 出自拉丁 substitutio，即 substituere「使替代、置于其位」的动作名词；substituere 由 sub-「在下、代替」与 statuere「安置、使站立」构成，而 statuere 又出自 stare「站立」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin statuere 'to set up, place, establish' comes from stare 'to stand' and supplies the idea of setting something in a position.
items.cn: 拉丁 statuere「竖立、安置、确立」出自 stare「站立」，提供「把某物放到某个位置」的思路。

items.en: substituere, from sub- 'under, in place of' plus statuere, meant 'to set in place of another, put under'.
items.cn: substituere 由 sub-「在下、代替」与 statuere 构成，意为「把一物置于另一物之位、置于其下」。

items.en: substitutio is the action noun of substituere, formed with -io; it names the act of setting one thing in another's place.
items.cn: substitutio 是 substituere 的动作名词，以 -io 构成，命名「把一物置于另一物之位」的动作。

items.en: Old French substitution and Latin substitutio supply the English noun in the fifteenth century; substitute appears first as a person and later as a verb.
items.cn: 古法语 substitution 与拉丁 substitutio 于十五世纪提供英语名词；substitute 先指人，后作动词。

items.en: Algebra, chemistry and team sport each took the word between the eighteenth and twentieth centuries because each turns a symbol, a group or a player into a replaceable slot.
items.cn: 代数、化学与团队运动在十八至二十世纪各自采用该词，因为它们都把符号、基团或球员变成可替换的位置。

items.en: The first English citation of substitution is uncertain. Latin sub- has several shades, 'under' and 'instead of' among them, and which shade is primary in substituere is a matter of interpretation rather than record; the Indo-European root of stare is reconstructed as *steh₂-.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：substitution 的英语最早书证年代不明。拉丁 sub- 有数种含义，「在下」与「代替」都在其中，substituere 中哪一义为主属解释问题而非文献记录；stare 的印欧词根被重构为 *steh₂-。

note.en: The first group separates the substitute family by part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms, with register and direction of change as the main differences.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 substitute 词族；第二组给出近义词，主要差别在语域与替换的方向性。

entries.definition: The stand-in or the act of standing in; substitution is the abstract noun for that act.
entries.definitionCN: 指替代者，或指代替的动作；substitution 是表示该动作的抽象名词。

entries.definition: Relating to substitution, common in legal and religious language; it modifies a noun rather than naming the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为与替换有关的，常见于法律与宗教语言；它修饰名词，而不是命名动作。

entries.definition: Capable of being replaced; it describes a property of the thing, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 意为可被替代的；它描述事物的属性，而不是事件。

entries.definition: Serving as a substitute; it describes the role something plays, not the act of change.
entries.definitionCN: 意为起替代作用的；它描述某物所扮演的角色，而不是替换动作。

entries.definition: The everyday word for putting a new thing in place, often permanently; substitution is more formal and technical, and is the usual term in maths, chemistry and sport.
entries.definitionCN: 指把新物放到原位的日常说法，常含永久替换之意；substitution 更正式、更技术化，是数学、化学与体育中的常用术语。

entries.definition: A casual exchange, often of two things traded for each other; substitution is one-directional and neutral in register.
entries.definitionCN: 指随意的交换，常为两物互换；substitution 是单向的，语域中性偏正式。

entries.definition: Giving one thing and receiving another; substitution need not involve anything coming back.
entries.definitionCN: 指给出一物并收到另一物；substitution 不一定涉及回返之物。

entries.definition: A person or thing acting in another's role, especially in medicine or law; it names the stand-in, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指代替他人角色的对象，尤用于医学或法律；它命名替代者，而不是替换行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sub- (in place of) + stitut (set, from statuere) + -ion: setting one thing in another's place.
normal.cn: sub-（代替）+ stitut（安置，出自 statuere）+ -ion：把一物置于另一物之位。

normal.en: The family runs substitute, substitution, substitutable, substitutional, substitutive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 substitute、substitution、substitutable、substitutional、substitutive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: substitution effect, substitution cipher, nucleophilic substitution, make a substitution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各领域：替代效应、替换密码、亲核取代、进行换人。

normal.en: A substitute is the stand-in; substitution is the change; substitutable is the property.
normal.cn: substitute 是替代者，substitution 是替换，substitutable 是可替代的性质。

normal.en: Replacement is plain and often permanent; substitution is formal, technical and slot-based.
normal.cn: replacement 平实且常指永久替换；substitution 正式、技术化，并以「位置」为核心。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece lifted and another set on the same square.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子被拿起，另一枚被放到同一个方格上。

abstract.en: Picture a form with a blank where a name can be written again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，留有一处可以重新写名字的空白。

abstract.en: Picture a tactics board with a numbered magnet carried from the bench to the pitch.
abstract.cn: 想象战术板上，一枚编号磁子从替补席被移到球场位置。

examples.en: The substitution of machine parts for manual checks speeded up production.
examples.cn: 用机器部件替代人工检查加快了生产。

examples.en: A substitution cipher hides the message by replacing each letter.
examples.cn: 替换密码通过替换每个字母来隐藏信息。

examples.en: The referee allowed the substitution after the injury.
examples.cn: 裁判在受伤后允许换人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub（下面／代替）+ stitution」——把另一个放到它的位置 → substitution 替换

root: 拉丁 stare「站立」→ 拉丁 statuere「安置、使站立」→ 拉丁 substituere「使替代、置于其位」→ 拉丁 substitutio → 英语 substitution。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one act, putting one thing in another's place: plain replacement, substitution into an equation, a group taking a site in a molecule, a player coming on, the substitution effect, a language slot, a cipher alphabet and a change of contract party.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一动作「把一物置于另一物之位」：一般替换、数学代入、化学基团顶替、球员上场、替代效应、语言位置、密码字母表，以及合同主体变更。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one piece is lifted and another set down on the same square.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚棋子被拿起，另一枚被放到同一个方格上。

branches.en: PLAIN AND CODED: one object or symbol takes another's place.
branches.cn: 一般与编码：一个物体或符号占据另一个的位置。

branches.en: FORMAL SYSTEMS: a value enters an equation, and a group takes a site on a molecule.
branches.cn: 形式系统：数值进入方程，基团占据分子上的位点。

branches.en: COUNTED SLOTS: a player and a basket position are swapped, with effects measured.
branches.cn: 可计数的位置：球员与篮子中的位置被替换，并计量其效应。

branches.en: THE LANGUAGE SLOT: a form is tested by what can stand in its position.
branches.cn: 语言位置：用一个形式能否占据该位置来检验它。

branches.en: THE LEGAL PARTY: the obligation stays, the person under it changes.
branches.cn: 法律主体：义务保留，承担义务的人发生变更。

intro.en: Substitution layers Latin sub- 'in place of', statuere 'to set', the action ending -io, and an English noun built on the Latin participle stem substitut-.
intro.cn: substitution 分层构成：拉丁 sub-「代替」、statuere「安置」、动作名词词尾 -io，以及建立在拉丁分词词干 substitut- 之上的英语名词。

latinIntro.en: statuere comes from stare 'to stand'; sub- adds the idea of placing under or instead, and -io forms the action noun substitutio, which reaches English as -tion.
latinIntro.cn: statuere 出自 stare「站立」；sub- 附加「置于其下或代替」之意，-io 构成动作名词 substitutio，经法语进入英语作 -tion。

items.meaning: the act of putting one thing in another's place
items.meaningCN: 把一物置于另一物之位的动作
items.example: No substitution of ingredients is allowed.

items.meaning: a stand-in, or to stand in
items.example: Honey can substitute for sugar in this recipe.
items.exampleCN: 在这个食谱里，蜂蜜可以代替糖。
这两个零件可以互换替代。

items.example: The doctrine is substitutional rather than penal.
items.exampleCN: 这一学说是替代性的，而非惩罚性的。

items.example: Substitutive therapy helps the body replace what it lacks.
items.exampleCN: 替代疗法帮助身体补足所缺之物。

items.meaning: the degree to which one thing can replace another
items.meaningCN: 一物可替代另一物的程度
items.example: Elasticity depends on the substitutability of the goods.
items.exampleCN: 弹性取决于商品之间的可替代性。
被取代的化合物表现出不同性质。

items.example: Substituting a symbol for a value is the first step.
items.exampleCN: 用符号代替数值是第一步。

latinEntries.meaning: to set one thing in place of another
latinEntries.meaningCN: 使替代；把一物置于另一物之位

definition_zh: 癫痫；癫痫症
definition_en: a brain disorder in which a person has repeated seizures caused by sudden electrical surges
core_image: 脑内一场毫无预告的雷暴，几分钟后云散雨停，患者醒过来却对刚才一无所知
scene: 体育课上老师解释同学的病情。 Epilepsy is a treatable brain disorder.
sceneCN: 这里 epilepsy 是「癫痫症」（第 1 个义项：反复抽搐发作的慢性脑病）；句意：癫痫是可以治疗的脑病。

pos.zh: 癫痫；癫痫症

senses.title: A chronic disorder of recurrent seizures
senses.definition: the medical condition marked by two or more unprovoked seizures over time
senses.definitionCN: 以两次以上无诱因发作为特征的医学病症
senses.example: Childhood epilepsy often settles with age.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童期癫痫常随年龄增长而缓解。
senses.why: The Greek stem says a seizure comes over a person from outside, like something grabbing hold.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词干说的是发作从外部攫住患者，如同被一只手抓住。

senses.title: The state of being liable to fits
senses.definition: the disposition that makes a person expect an attack without warning
senses.definitionCN: 使人无从预告便预期发作的身体倾向
senses.example: Stress can worsen epilepsy.
senses.exampleCN: 压力会使癫痫加重。
senses.why: Clinical prose uses the noun for the tendency itself, not only for the diagnosed disease.
senses.whyCN: 临床书写用该名词指倾向本身，而不止指确诊之病。

senses.title: The disease once called sacred
senses.definition: the historical name for a condition attributed to divine visitation or the moon
senses.definitionCN: 历史上把此病归因于神罚或月象的旧称
senses.example: Ancient writers feared epilepsy as a heaven-sent blow.
senses.exampleCN: 古人视癫痫为天降一击而心生畏惧。
senses.why: Hippocrates argued against that reading, and the word survived with the argument attached.
senses.whyCN: 希波克拉底反驳这一解释，词语连同那段辩论一并留存至今。

intro.en: Epilepsy is Greek for a seizing, from epi- upon plus lambanein to take hold.
intro.cn: epilepsy 在希腊语中意为被攫住，由 epi-「在上」与 lambanein「抓住」合成。

items.en: Lambanein means to take or seize.
items.cn: lambanein 意为抓取。

items.en: Epilambanein means to come over someone and seize them.
items.cn: epilambanein 意为临身攫人。

items.en: Epilepsia named the disease that falls upon a person.
items.cn: epilepsia 命名了骤然临身的疾病。

items.en: Hippocratic writing rejected the label of sacred disease.
items.cn: 希波克拉底文献否定了圣病这一标签。

items.en: Epilepsia passed through medical Latin and French epilepsie.
items.cn: epilepsia 经医学拉丁语与法语 epilepsie 转手。

items.en: Neurology fixed the definition on recurrent unprovoked seizures.
items.cn: 现代神经病学把它界定为反复无诱因发作。

note.en: Group one holds words sharing the Greek ending for a seizing; group two holds other words for sudden loss of control.
note.cn: 第一组共用希腊语表攫获的词尾；第二组是其他表骤然失控的词。

entries.definition: Describes the attack or the person who has attacks.
entries.definitionCN: 既可修饰发作，也可指患者本人。

entries.definition: Sudden sleep attacks, built on numbness plus seizing.
entries.definitionCN: 骤然入睡之症，由麻痹加攫获构成。

entries.definition: A neurologist who concentrates on seizure disorders.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻发作性疾病的神经科医生。

entries.definition: A stroke, from the same Greek family of striking down.
entries.definitionCN: 中风旧称，同出希腊语击倒一词族。

entries.definition: One attack, used whether or not the disease is chronic.
entries.definitionCN: 单次发作，无论是否慢性病均可使用。

entries.definition: Violent involuntary contraction of the muscles.
entries.definitionCN: 肌肉剧烈的不自主收缩。

entries.definition: The plain household term for an attack.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中对发作的称呼。

entries.definition: A brief loss of consciousness without electrical storm.
entries.definitionCN: 短暂失去意识而无异常放电。

normalIntro.en: Epilepsy names the condition; seizure names one episode of it.
normalIntro.cn: epilepsy 指病症本身，seizure 指其中一次发作。

normal.en: Treat it as uncountable and use no article before the bare noun.
normal.cn: 作不可数名词，裸形前不加冠词。

normal.en: Say a child with epilepsy, not an epilepsy.
normal.cn: 说 a child with epilepsy，不说 an epilepsy。

normal.en: Pair with verbs such as diagnose, control, manage.
normal.cn: 搭配 diagnose、control、manage 等动词。

normal.en: The adjective epileptic modifies seizure or attack.
normal.cn: 形容词 epileptic 修饰 seizure 或 attack。

normal.en: Avoid outdated slang in essays and reports.
normal.cn: 写作与报道中回避过时俗称。

abstract.en: Picture a lightswitch thrown by someone else's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象电闸被另一只手猛地拉下。

abstract.en: Imagine a storm cell crossing one field in a wide plain, then moving on.
abstract.cn: 想象雷雨云团扫过平原上的一小块田地，随即远去。

abstract.en: Think of a video that skips for a minute and then resumes.
abstract.cn: 想想一段跳掉一分钟又继续播放的录像。

examples.en: She was diagnosed with epilepsy at nine.
examples.cn: 她九岁时被确诊患有癫痫。

examples.en: New drugs keep many cases of epilepsy under control.
examples.cn: 新药使许多癫痫病例得到控制。

examples.en: The syllabus now explains epilepsy to younger pupils.
examples.cn: 教学大纲如今向低龄学生讲解癫痫知识。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一劈雷熄」——发作时像被雷劈倒，一番抽搐后又如雷声熄灭般醒转，所以 epilepsy 是癫痫；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 epi-（在上、临身）＋ lambanein（抓取）→ epilambanein（临身攫人）→ epilepsia（被攫住之病）→ 拉丁语 epilepsia → 法语 epilepsie → 英语 epilepsy，核心义「从外面抓住患者的病」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun covers the diagnosed disease, the tendency to attack, and the older sacred-disease idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词涵盖确诊之病、发作倾向，以及圣病的旧观念。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something outside the body takes hold of a person for a few minutes.
core.cn: 核心意象：体外之力将人攫住几分钟，随后松手。

branches.en: Medicine counts the attacks to name the disease.
branches.cn: 医学以发作次数界定病症。

branches.en: The body keeps a standing liability to be grabbed.
branches.cn: 身体保有被攫住的持续可能。

branches.en: Older cultures blamed powers from above.
branches.cn: 古代文化把病因归于上天之力。

branches.en: Both describe the electrical event, not its explanation.
branches.cn: 两者都描述放电事件而非其解释。

branches.en: Both treat the sufferer as acted upon rather than acting.
branches.cn: 两者都把患者视为被作用者而非施动者。

intro.en: A Greek prefix of position joins a verb of seizing, and the disease takes a noun ending.
intro.cn: 希腊语表位置的前缀接上表抓取的动词，病症再带名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek lambanein is to take, and the prefix keeps its Greek shape epi-.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 lambanein 表抓取，拉丁语一侧则常见前缀 epi-。

items.example: Epi- marks the power coming over.
The ending closes the disease name.

items.exampleCN: narco- 加 lepsy 构成嗜睡症。
apo- 加 plexy 构成中风一词。

definition_zh: 声学专家；声学工程师；建筑声学顾问
definition_en: a specialist who studies or works with sound, especially in buildings, music or the environment
core_image: 一人拿着测声仪站在音乐厅空荡的座位间
scene: 音乐厅还没开门，空座之间已经有人拿着仪器走动。 The acoustician measured how sound travelled through the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 acoustician 是「声学专家」（第 1 个义项：研究或处理声音的专门人才）；句意为这位声学专家测量声音在大厅中如何传播。

pos.zh: 名词：声学专家；声学工程师

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「听觉」词根加 -ics 构成的学科名，义为「声学；音响效果」
由希腊语「听觉」词根加 -ic 构成，义为「声学的；原声的」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「在声学上；从声音角度」
由 acoustic 加 -al 构成的形容词变体，义为「声学的」

senses.title: A specialist in acoustics
senses.definition: a person trained in the science of sound and vibration
senses.definitionCN: 受过声音与振动科学训练的人
senses.example: The acoustician explained why the room amplified every whisper.
senses.exampleCN: 这位声学专家解释了为什么这间屋子会放大每句耳语。
senses.why: Acoustics is the science of hearing, and -ician marks a practitioner, so the word names the person who works with sound as a science.
senses.whyCN: acoustics 是研究听觉的科学，-ician 标记从业者，所以这个词指把声音当作科学研究的人。

senses.title: An architectural acoustics consultant
senses.definition: a professional who advises architects on how a building will carry, absorb or isolate sound
senses.definitionCN: 就建筑如何传导、吸收或隔绝声音向建筑师提供建议的专业人士
senses.example: The acoustician recommended thicker walls around the rehearsal room.
senses.exampleCN: 声学顾问建议在排练室周围使用更厚的墙。
senses.why: Buildings are one of the largest practical problems in sound, so the specialist is often hired at the design stage.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是声音最大的实际问题之一，所以这位专家常在设计阶段就被聘用。

senses.title: A noise-control engineer
senses.definition: an engineer who reduces unwanted noise in machines, workplaces or cities
senses.definitionCN: 降低机器、工作场所或城市中不需要的噪声的工程师
senses.example: The acoustician traced the factory noise to a badly mounted fan.
senses.exampleCN: 这位噪声控制工程师把工厂噪声追查到一台安装不良的风扇。
senses.why: The same science is turned toward removing sound rather than designing it, which is the noise-control branch.
senses.whyCN: 同一门科学被用来消除声音而不是设计声音，这就是噪声控制分支。

senses.title: A researcher in musical acoustics
senses.definition: a scientist who studies how instruments and voices produce and shape sound
senses.definitionCN: 研究乐器与人声如何产生并塑造声音的科学家
senses.example: The acoustician built a model of how the violin body resonates.
senses.exampleCN: 这位声学专家建立了一个模型，说明小提琴琴身如何共振。
senses.why: Music gives sound a precise structure, so the specialist can measure pitch, resonance and timbre in controlled ways.
senses.whyCN: 音乐给声音提供了精确结构，所以专家能以受控方式测量音高、共振与音色。

senses.title: An underwater acoustics expert
senses.definition: a specialist in how sound travels through water, used in sonar and marine research
senses.definitionCN: 研究声音如何在水中传播的专家，应用于声呐与海洋研究
senses.example: The navy consulted an acoustician before changing its sonar frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 海军在改变声呐频率前咨询了一位水声学专家。
senses.why: Water carries sound very differently from air, so the general science grows a separate underwater branch.
senses.whyCN: 水传播声音的方式与空气很不同，所以这门总体科学分出了独立的水下分支。

senses.title: An environmental noise assessor
senses.definition: a person who measures and assesses noise impact on neighbourhoods and wildlife
senses.definitionCN: 测量并评估噪声对社区与野生动物影响的人
senses.example: The acoustician mapped the noise from the new motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 这位声学专家绘制了新高速公路的噪声分布图。
senses.why: Once noise is treated as pollution, the specialist is needed to measure it and argue about limits.
senses.whyCN: 一旦噪声被当作污染，就需要专家来测量它并讨论限值。

senses.title: A teacher of acoustics
senses.definition: a person who teaches acoustics to students of physics, engineering or music
senses.definitionCN: 向物理、工程或音乐专业学生教授声学的人
senses.example: As an acoustician, she taught a course on room design.
senses.exampleCN: 作为声学专家，她讲授一门关于房间设计的课程。
senses.why: A specialist can also be the one who passes the science on, so the word covers the teaching role.
senses.whyCN: 专家也可以是把这门科学传下去的人，所以这个词也涵盖教学角色。

senses.title: A sound-system designer
senses.definition: a person who designs or tunes sound systems and listening spaces for clear, even sound
senses.definitionCN: 设计或调试音响系统与聆听空间，使声音清晰均匀的人
senses.example: The acoustician tuned the concert hall speakers before the tour opened.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演开始前，这位声学专家调试了音乐厅的扬声器。
senses.why: The practical end of the science is making a space sound right, which joins measurement with design.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学的实践终点是让空间听起来正确，于是测量与设计在此汇合。

intro.en: Acoustician is a nineteenth-century English formation on the Greek verb for hearing, with the practitioner suffix -ician.
intro.cn: acoustician 是十九世纪在希腊语「听」动词基础上构成的英语词，加上表示从业者的后缀 -ician。

items.en: Greek akouein meant to hear; its deeper Indo-European connections are reconstructed and in part source uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 akouein 意为「听见」；其更早的印欧语关联属重构，部分来源不确定。

items.en: Akoustikos meant of or for hearing, and it was used of sounds and of the sense itself.
items.cn: akoustikos 意为「与听觉有关的、为听觉的」，用于声音也用于听觉本身。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as acusticus, keeping the hearing sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词作 acusticus，保留「听觉」之意。

items.en: French acoustique carried the word into modern European languages, where it also named the science.
items.cn: 法语 acoustique 把这个词带入现代欧洲语言，并同时用来指这门科学。

items.en: English acoustic is recorded from the seventeenth century; acoustics as a science name followed later.
items.cn: 英语 acoustic 在十七世纪已有记录；作为学科名的 acoustics 更晚出现。

items.en: Acoustician was formed with -ician on the model of musician and physician; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: acoustician 仿 musician、physician 等词加上 -ician 构成，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the acoustics family; the near-meaning group gathers other sound professionals and hearing specialists.
note.cn: 形近组收 acoustics 词族；近义组收其他声音从业者与听觉专家。

entries.definition: The science of sound, or the sound properties of a room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声学」或「空间的音响效果」，是本词的学科基础。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to sound, or describing an instrument that is not amplified.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「声音的」，也指不靠电声放大的原声乐器。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in terms of sound or acoustics.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从声学角度、在声音方面」。

entries.definition: An adjective variant of acoustic, common in engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是 acoustic 的变体，工程文献中常见。

entries.definition: A compound job title close in meaning to acoustician but marked as engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 复合职位名，意义接近 acoustician，但更强调工程身份。

entries.definition: A hearing-health professional who tests and treats human hearing, not building sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「听力师」，测试与治疗人的听力，不处理建筑声学。

entries.definition: A person who records, mixes or reproduces sound; practical rather than scientific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「音响工程师」，负责录音、混音或重放，偏实操而非科研。

entries.definition: A scientist of matter and energy; acoustics is one branch of physics.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物理学家」，研究物质与能量；声学是物理学的分支之一。

entries.definition: A person who operates underwater sound equipment rather than studying sound in general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声呐技师」，操作水下声学设备，而非研究一般声音。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek hearing root and the real job compounds the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用希腊语「听」词根，以及这个词实际出现的职业复合词。

normal.en: Greek akouein means to hear, so acoustics is literally the study of hearing.
normal.cn: 希腊语 akouein 意为「听见」，所以 acoustics 字面上就是研究听觉。

normal.en: The -ician ending marks a practitioner, as in musician and physician.
normal.cn: -ician 结尾标记从业者，如 musician 与 physician。

normal.en: An architectural acoustician is hired before a hall is built, not after.
normal.cn: 建筑声学专家在音乐厅建成之前就被聘用，而不是建成之后。

normal.en: Underwater acoustics is a separate branch because water carries sound differently.
normal.cn: 水声学是独立分支，因为水传播声音的方式不同。

normal.en: The opposite job is noise control, where the same science removes sound.
normal.cn: 相对的工作是噪声控制，用同一门科学去消除声音。

abstract.en: Picture an empty concert hall: one person walks the aisles with a meter while the seats stay silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一座空音乐厅：一个人拿着仪表走过走道，座位一片寂静。

abstract.en: The acoustician does not make music; they make the room behave so music can be heard.
abstract.cn: 声学专家不创作音乐；他们让房间规矩起来，好让音乐被听见。

abstract.en: Sound is invisible, so the specialist's real tool is measurement, not the ear alone.
abstract.cn: 声音看不见，所以专家真正的工具是测量，而不只是耳朵。

examples.en: The acoustician spent three days testing the new lecture hall.
examples.cn: 这位声学专家花了三天测试新的讲堂。

examples.en: Before the concert, an acoustician adjusted the ceiling panels.
examples.cn: 音乐会前，一位声学专家调整了天花板板件。

examples.en: The city hired an acoustician to study traffic noise near the school.
examples.cn: 市里聘请一位声学专家研究学校附近的交通噪声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿库斯提申」——阿库斯提着仪器，一间间屋子听：声学专家

root: 希腊语 akouein「听见」派生出 akoustikos「与听觉有关的」，经拉丁语 acusticus 与法语 acoustique 进入英语；英语再加 -ician「从业者」构成 acoustician。更早的印欧语关联属重构，部分来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow one trained listener into different rooms: pure science, building design, noise control, music, underwater sound, environmental assessment, teaching, and sound-system tuning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一位受过训练的「听者」走进不同场所：纯科学、建筑设计、噪声控制、音乐、水下声音、环境评估、教学，以及音响系统调试。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a sound meter stands in an empty hall, listening to how the room answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着声级计站在空荡的大厅里，听房间如何回应。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the specialist knows the subject and can teach it.
branches.cn: 科学线：专家掌握这门学科，也能教授它。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: halls and sound systems are designed so that listening works.
branches.cn: 建筑线：大厅与音响系统被设计成让聆听成立。

branches.en: THE NUISANCE: the same knowledge is used to measure and reduce unwanted sound.
branches.cn: 扰民线：同样的知识被用来测量并减少不需要的声音。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: music provides precise sound to study and tune.
branches.cn: 乐器线：音乐提供精确的声音供研究与调试。

branches.en: THE SEA: water turns sound into a separate technical branch.
branches.cn: 海洋线：水使声音分出一个独立的技术分支。

intro.en: The word joins a Greek hearing root with a Latin-derived practitioner suffix; the science name and the person name grew side by side.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语「听」词根与源自拉丁的从业者后缀连接起来；学科名与人名是并行长出的。

latinIntro.en: Greek akouein and akoustikos are recorded, and Latin acusticus borrowed the adjective; no native Latin root is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 akouein 与 akoustikos 均有记录，拉丁语 acusticus 借入了这个形容词；不涉及拉丁本族词根。

items.example: It is the hearing element in the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族中的「听」元素。

items.example: It appears in sonar, a related sound technology.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 sonar 这一相关声音技术中。
